ca23cb24e7dac3b1: Milburn’s review is considering how to address the growing number of young people classified as not in education, employment or training Here are more quotes from what Alan Milburn told the Times about the proposals in his youth unemployment report, which is being published next week. Milburn said he concluded fundamental change was needed. He said: The whole system needs to be changed, because the system is geared to keeping people inactive when, for young people in particular, it’s all about how can you make them active, get them earning, learning, so that they can rely on a wage rather than on a benefit. So, this is not about cutting one benefit, it’s about rebuilding the system from scratch. He said that he decided existing claimants should be covered by the changes, not just new changes. It’s a big rewriting of the welfare system. And obviously one of the conundrums was, ‘Should this apply to only new claimants?’ I came to the conclusion that wouldn’t be right, not least because you’ve got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job. Milburn admitted this meant the plans would not be “pain-free”. I’m not saying that any of this will be easy or that it will be pain-free because it won’t. You know, candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. He said he wanted the system to prioritise improving people’s life chances in the long term over easing their financial hardship in the short term. Actually for young people there’s a different debate that we’ve got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. I think what the current system does, it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that’s the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around. He said, alongside the cuts to benefits he is proposing (see 11.56am), he wanted to improve employment support for young people. We need to make sure people have the opportunities to get an apprenticeship, a job, a work placement, a pre-apprenticeship, a college place. The menu of opportunities has got to increase. They’ll have a personal adviser, they’ll be coached all the way through. The adviser will stick with them until they have found a job or an apprenticeship or college place. He also confirmed he wants to let young people do some work before they start losing benefits. They will get immediate access to support if that’s what they need, if that’s the thing that is holding them back from being in education or training. He admitted that offering better employment support and mental health support would mean his plans would initially cost money. According to the Times, he did not did not deny claims the whole package could cost £6bn. But, in the long run, there would be savings, he said. Obviously this costs money. And frankly it’s a better use of money, both from the point of view of the young person and the taxpayer, to spend that money getting them into work rather than spending that money keeping them on benefits. This is the sort of fatuous thing about this debate. You’ve got to invest upfront in order to get savings out of the back end. Cost-free is fatuous. So we’ve got to be candid about that. It will need significant investment. To get a return on investment will take time … the only way of cutting the benefits bill sustainably is by getting young people into work, paying their taxes and being less reliant on benefits. Unless you are prepared to put the investment upfront it will never be possible. He said he was “confident” that Andy Burnham was full-square behind the changes that are needed.” Under [Milburn’s] proposals, young people aged 18 to 24 would be barred from claiming the two main sickness and disability benefits: the health element of universal credit and personal independence payments (Pip). They would instead be given a new youth allowance, which would be paid at the standard rate of universal credit, while billions would be invested in one-to-one employment support to get them into work. a33dc3f7bc0a22fa: MELAKA: Bersatu has described the encouraging response from voters in the seven state constituencies it is contesting in the Melaka election as a positive sign ahead of polling day on Saturday.

be62eca10e38115e: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) can now issue flood warnings up to one hour in advance, compared with just five minutes previously, following upgrades to the Kuala Lumpur Command Centre.
Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui said the command centre's enhanced capabilities allow residents to be alerted much earlier.
He said 14 flood and flash flood hotspots had been identified in Kuala Lumpur this year, though none were located within the Batu parliamentary constituency.

"Based on records from the past five years, two locations in the Batu parliamentary constituency, Kampung Chubadak Asal and Kampung Seri Delima, have experienced flash floods, affecting a total of 250 residents," he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was replying to a question from Prabakaran M. Parameswaran (PH-Batu) on the number of residents living in flood-prone areas in Batu, the capacity of temporary evacuation centres (PPS) and the government's plans to provide medium-term temporary accommodation.
Lo said DBKL and the Social Welfare Department had coordinated 36 temporary evacuation centres with a combined capacity of 3,550 people as part of short- and medium-term measures.
On the challenges faced, he said about 70 per cent of Kuala Lumpur's original 33.5 hectares of water catchment or retention areas had been lost due to previous land alienation.
However, he said DBKL and the Federal Territories Department were working with the Selangor government to identify suitable sites for replacement retention ponds.

"In addition, the Federal Territories Department and DBKL have frozen development applications involving land on or around retention ponds and are planning to transform Kuala Lumpur into a sponge city.
"We will continue to improve DBKL's performance, particularly in tackling flooding in Kuala Lumpur," he said.

98e701325e59d07e: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is expanding its computer laboratory device rental services to 1,801 schools that lack such facilities to ensure comprehensive access to digital learning resources.

The ministry said the expansion began in the third quarter of this year as a key approach to strengthening digital facilities in schools, alongside the targeted distribution of devices to students from the low-income (B40) group.

It said the supply of computer laboratory devices was implemented in three phases from 2021 to 2023, involving the distribution of 244,158 devices to schools nationwide, regardless of location or parliamentary constituency.

To support B40 and rural students, the ministry, through Yayasan Didik Negara, also distributed 16,230 free digital education devices—comprising laptops, Chromebooks and tablets—to 257 schools nationwide between 2022 and 2026.

"This free device distribution is carried out in a targeted and transparent manner, based on needs-based criteria verified by the State Education Departments (JPN) and District Education Offices (PPD)," it said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.

The ministry was replying to a question from Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Hussein (BN-Sembrong) on the status of free digital device distribution to B40 students in rural areas and plans for high-performance internet coverage in remote school laboratories.

To improve internet access in schools, including in remote areas, the ministry provides fibre-optic facilities with speeds ranging from 300 Mbps to 800 Mbps and broadband services at 30 Mbps. Schools facing limitations in accessing terrestrial networks are provided with high-performance satellite internet services offering speeds of up to 100 Mbps.
As of October this year, 8,955 schools (87.28 per cent) out of 10,259 MOE educational institutions nationwide had internet access through fibre-optic technology, the ministry said.
The remaining institutions, which still rely on wireless broadband and satellite technology, are being upgraded in phases based on technical feasibility at their respective locations.
e08f4ba3a81ccf13: BANGI, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision.

“But I have always stressed that when we speak of matters under Article 42, it is considered what is referred to as the prerogative of mercy, which we know is among the powers fully vested in the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the power of pardon.
“So it is up to the Malaysian Bar as to what it wants to bring... If the Malaysian Bar feels it has the right to question any issue, that is its right,” she told reporters here today.

She said this after the certificate presentation ceremony for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and Mediator Appointment Certificates, as well as the launch of the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, Legal Aid Department 2026.

The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) today objected to the Malaysian Bar’s bid to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.

Senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly@Arwi informed High Court Judge S. Indra Nehru today that the AGC had received the Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review by email two days earlier and needed time to file written submissions.

Meanwhile, Najib’s lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee informed the court that his client also intended to file written submissions, as any decision by the court after leave is granted could affect him.
Lawyer Zainur Zakaria, representing the Malaysian Bar, did not object to the requests by the AGC and Najib’s lawyers for time to file their respective written submissions.

Judge Indra Nehru fixed March 17 next year to hear the application and directed both parties to file their respective written submissions by December 14, with replies to be filed on or before December 28.

On November 10, the Bar filed the judicial review application naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents. — Bernama

26e1e8f2dc6d28fb: BEIJING: Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China, worried that the scandal involving the US chipmaker's CEO Jensen Huang could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors, three people familiar with the matter said.

Seeking to protect US dominance of the critical sector, Washington restricts exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips. But Chinese companies can access such processors remotely by renting computing power at data centres overseas.
The current move to secure rented capacity points to growing concern among Chinese technology companies that the gap in US export controls may now be closed.

A major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have contacted data-centre operators about reserving it, the people said. The people declined to be identified, or to identify the cloud provider, due to the sensitivity of the matter.
Smaller AI labs are considering similar steps, including approaching major providers of rented computing power in Southeast Asia, two of the people said.

The companies fear the controversy surrounding Huang could add political momentum to the Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, a US bill that would give the Commerce Department authority to regulate remote, cloud-based access to restricted technology, the people said. The House of Representatives passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and it awaits Senate action.

Advanced Nvidia processors are used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products. Restricting overseas cloud access would make it harder for Chinese developers to obtain high-end computing power without importing the chips directly.
CHINESE SPY ALLEGATIONS TRIGGER US SCRUTINY

Nvidia's Huang said on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times reported that the woman involved was Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed, and that US authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. Jensen and Alice Huang are not related.
Reuters could not independently verify that allegation, which China has denied.

Megaspeed has faced scrutiny from US authorities over suspicions it helped Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips that were subject to US export controls. The company has denied illegally diverting chips to China.

In a statement on Thursday, Megaspeed said it had cooperated with inspections by the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security and hired a leading US law firm to conduct a comprehensive inventory of its graphics processing units and independently verify its export-control compliance practices.
It said it welcomed government scrutiny and was committed to complying with US export-control laws.
Nvidia and the US Commerce Department did not respond to requests for comment.

Shares of Chinese AI companies fell sharply in Hong Kong on Thursday amid concerns that the controversy could lead to tighter US restrictions on access to advanced chips. Alibaba fell as much as 7.1 per cent while AI model developers Z.AI and MiniMax both dropped at least 7.0 per cent.
Alice Huang had business dealings and investment ties with several leading Chinese technology companies, including Tencent and Alibaba, according to two people familiar with the matter.
Tencent said its computing procurement, leasing and operations complied with applicable laws and regulations, including export controls.

"We have no knowledge of, nor involvement in, any alleged unlawful activities referenced in these reports, nor do we have any business dealings or investment ties with the individuals concerned," the company said.
Alibaba did not respond to a request for comment.
GREY-MARKET BUYING SURGES AMID FEARS OF SMUGGLING CRACKDOWN

The prospect of tougher enforcement has also fuelled demand for restricted Nvidia AI chips in China's grey market, prompting traders and intermediaries to start stockpiling these processors, two of the people said.
They said buyers fear the controversy could prompt a broader US crackdown on smuggling of advanced chips and AI servers into China.

A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology.

US prosecutors in March charged Super Micro Computer co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and two others with conspiring to divert servers containing Nvidia chips to China through a Southeast Asia-based company.

Prosecutors said the company bought about US$2.5 billion of servers from Super Micro between 2024 and 2025, and that a substantial portion was diverted to China. The defendants have not been convicted.

0c42e9019c05f619: PENDANG: Four men were arrested after their car skidded into a drain while fleeing police in Jalan Kampung Bendang Raja, Kubur Panjang, here yesterday.
In the 6.30pm incident, the Proton Persona carrying the four suspects, aged between 33 and 51, failed to stop when ordered by police.

District police chief Superintendent Rodzi Abu Hassan said the driver sped off and swerved into a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) from the Pendang police headquarters' Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department, causing the two vehicles to graze each other before the car skidded into a drain on the left side of the road.
He said checks found all four local men injured, and they were taken to Pendang Hospital for treatment.

"Further checks on the suspects and their vehicle uncovered six transparent plastic packets of various sizes suspected to contain syabu and one transparent plastic packet suspected to contain heroin," he said in a statement today.
Rodzi said background checks showed the 48-year-old suspect had a criminal record with 15 prior offences, while the 51-year-old had five.
The other two suspects, aged 34 and 33, had two prior criminal offences each, he added.
"Initial urine screening tests found all of them positive for amphetamine, methamphetamine and morphine.

"Three suspects have been remanded for four days from today until Nov 15 under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to assist in the investigation, while the remaining suspect was released on police bail due to health reasons," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Section 186 of the Penal Code, and Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
177d02ea5ec6cf87: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The public can start activating the MyKomuter50 Pass on November 16 to enjoy unlimited travel for 30 days on selected KTM Komuter services for RM50, with savings of up to 88 per cent, effective December 1.
In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said the pass, aimed at easing the cost of living, was particularly beneficial to those commuting to work and educational institutions.

For example, users travelling on the Tanjung Malim-KL Sentral route, who would normally spend RM416 on fares over 30 days, would only need to pay RM50 with the pass, saving RM366 or nearly 88 per cent.
“For the Alor Setar-Butterworth route, users can save up to RM234, or about 82 per cent, compared with the estimated regular fare of RM284 over the same period and frequency of travel,” KTMB said.
The pass is open to Malaysian citizens aged seven and above who are not holders of the MyRailLife Pass. Applicants must present their MyKad or MyKid for eligibility verification.
Verification can be done through the KTM Mobile or KITS Style applications by uploading a copy of the identification document, a process that may take up to three working days.
Alternatively, users can obtain immediate verification at ticket kiosks or counters at KTM Komuter stations.

KTMB said activation and purchase facilities would be available at 34 selected stations, comprising 10 KTM Komuter Northern Sector stations, 20 Klang Valley KTM Komuter stations and four Southern Shuttle stations. An additional 11 registration counters would also be provided.
The pass is available at RM50 for each of the three service categories, namely MyKomuter50 Northern Sector, MyKomuter50 Klang Valley and MyKomuter50 Southern Shuttle.
KTMB encouraged users to complete the eligibility verification, activation and purchase processes on the same day.
Further information is available at www.ktmb.com.my or through the KTMB Call Centre at 03-9779 1200. — Bernama

19e5748593ad081f: LONDON: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after an eight-game winless Premier League run. The 45-year-old was their seventh permanent boss since Alex Ferguson retired after guiding the club to their last league title in 2013.
Following is a list of permanent and interim managers who have taken charge at United following Ferguson's retirement:
Former Everton manager Moyes struggled to fill Ferguson's shoes as defending champions United suffered with inconsistency, finishing seventh in the Premier League.
It was the first major coaching assignment for United's former midfielder Giggs, who holds the club's appearance record of 963. He remained at United as an assistant coach until 2016.
Dutchman Van Gaal arrived at United as one of the most respected managers of his generation, with successful spells at Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Ajax Amsterdam and the Netherlands over two decades.
United's performances improved and they finished fourth in 2014-15. But Van Gaal's possession-heavy playing style was criticised and he was fired two days after winning the FA Cup.
Trophies won: 3 (Europa League, League Cup, Community Shield)

Mourinho's arrival reflected United's ambition and his tenure got off to an optimistic start, with the team winning the League Cup and Europa League in his first campaign, followed by a second-place finish in the Premier League the next season.
Despite United spending nearly £400 million ($534.28 million) on players, a drop in performances in 2018-19 led to his dismissal when the team were 19 points off top spot.
In charge: December 19, 2018 (On interim basis, made permanent in March 2019) - November 21, 2021 (35 months)
Former United forward Solskjaer coached the club's reserve side from 2008-2011. He also managed Cardiff City and Norwegian club Molde before being appointed United's interim boss.

Solskjaer won 14 of his 19 matches before being made permanent manager but inconsistency plagued United for the rest of his stay. The Norwegian was dismissed after a string of losses including against Liverpool, Manchester City and Watford.
Former United midfielder Carrick was part of the club's coaching staff when appointed caretaker manager for less than two weeks, marking the start of his managerial career.
Rangnick attempted to steady the ship during a difficult season with underwhelming results as United came sixth in the Premier League and exited the Champions League in the last 16.
Ten Hag arrived at United following a successful spell at Ajax but, despite winning the League Cup and securing a top-four finish in his first season, his tenure took a downward turn.
United came eighth in 2023-24 but the Dutchman was given a second chance after winning the FA Cup. United were sitting 14th in October 2024 when he was fired.
Former United and Netherlands striker Van Nistelrooy, who joined the club as an assistant coach in July 2024, went unbeaten in four matches in all competitions as interim boss.
Amorim, who led Sporting to two Primeira Liga titles, had an unwavering commitment to an expansive 3-4-3 system built on intense pressing and possession-based football.
The 39-year-old became United's youngest manager since Wilf McGuinness took charge at 31 in 1969, but his spell ended after a poor run of results and public clashes.
Former United player Fletcher took charge of two matches, a Premier League draw with Burnley and an FA Cup defeat by Brighton & Hove Albion.
Former United and England midfielder Carrick was appointed on an interim basis before being handed a contract until 2028 after winning 11 of his first 16 matches.
Under Carrick, United climbed to third in the top flight and secured qualification for the Champions League.
However, he proved unable to carry that momentum into the new season and was dismissed after an eight-game Premier League winless streak. - Reuters
6c9dd5936403d0c8: MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined the coalition’s campaign trail in Melaka today as campaigning intensified ahead of Saturday’s state election.

802972f836853e84: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has allocated RM208.319 million next year to strengthen irrigation and drainage systems in Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) areas, including upgrading works, developing new water sources and rehabilitating the Pedu Dam in Kedah.

Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the initiative aims to ensure more efficient water resource management, particularly in tackling unpredictable rainfall patterns and lower reservoir levels compared with previous years.
He said Mada is also enhancing water resource monitoring through a telemetry system to continuously track reservoir levels, rainfall distribution and resource changes to guide management planning.

"In addition, the efficiency of the irrigation system is being improved through the operation of 117 water reuse pumps, maximising rainwater utilisation, water-flow control, as well as the maintenance of water control structures to ensure more efficient water distribution," he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was replying to a question from Datuk Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang) on the government's plans to strengthen irrigation and drainage systems in Mada areas to address unpredictable rainfall and low dam water levels.

Chan said the government is also adjusting padi planting schedules and practices based on water availability, promoting drought-resistant padi varieties and implementing six rounds of Cloud Seeding Operations (OPA) throughout 2026.

These measures are supported by the development and maintenance of 15 Tertiary Blocks and the Jeniang Water Transfer Scheme, which is expected to be completed by 2030 through a public-private partnership.

Replying to a supplementary question from Awang on the progress of tertiary irrigation projects and flood complaints in the Tokai area, Chan said Phase One of the project, involving 12 blocks, had recorded 25.81 per cent physical progress as of Oct 26, exceeding its 25.19 per cent target.
This puts the project 0.62 percentage points ahead of schedule, with full completion expected by 2030, he said.

On allegations that inadequate drainage had caused water to enter homes in the area, he said the ministry will instruct Mada officers to visit the affected locations to monitor the situation and gather direct feedback from residents.
89d1134d907fe879: KUALA LUMPUR: Ahead of its debut on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Nov 17, MyDCD Bhd reported a net profit of RM25.71 million on revenue of RM178.68 million for its first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), supported by strong contributions from its data centre infrastructure business.

The investment holding company, which operates through its subsidiary DCD Technology Sdn Bhd, recorded a profit before tax of RM34.06 million and gross profit of RM37.79 million for its first interim quarterly financial report.
As at Sept 30, 2026, MyDCD had an outstanding order book of approximately RM1.32 billion, providing earnings visibility as it continues to execute its secured projects.

Of the total, RM1.27 billion came from the integration of mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection (MEPF) systems for data centres, which is expected to be recognised progressively until the financial year ending June 30, 2028.
The remaining RM53.08 million comprised maintenance services and parts, with revenue recognition expected to extend until FY32.
The group said its data centre MEPF integration business accounted for approximately 96.85 per cent of total revenue during the quarter, reflecting its focus on critical infrastructure.

555c0bc21f885b90: Encountered some odd SQL Server connection behavior since the October update? There might be a culprit… Microsoft has admitted that a change has caused linked server queries to fail to close connections.

Linked servers via OLE DB providers have been around for years and are a useful way of, for example, using additional data sources in queries. Once a provider is added, SQL Server can open a connection to grab data, and close it again when the query is complete. Or, at least, that's the theory.

The problem is that after the October 13 (KB5126646) update, connections created by SQL Server linked server queries might remain open. According to Microsoft, "As additional queries are performed, connections to external databases can accumulate instead of closing as expected.
"This can slow or degrade server performance after prolonged run time."
You think? Administrators will likely have already noted a suspicious number of open connections to external databases on affected systems.

Microsoft said the issue affects SQL Server linked server queries that use OLE DB providers to connect to external databases. It gave PostgreSQL and Oracle as examples of connections known to be affected.
And the fix? "If idle connections can be identified, it is possible to manually close them to temporarily relieve server load.
"It is also possible to temporarily restore system stability by restarting the SQL service."
The Windows behemoth went on to state the obvious: "However, these steps can also interrupt active queries or transactions, and the problem can resurface again after sufficient operation time."

Bouncing a SQL Server to deal with connection leakage is less than ideal, although it would at least be a good failover test and, let's face it, having to restart Microsoft services regularly is something many administrators will be all too familiar with.
There is a mitigation available, although only through Microsoft support for business. Otherwise, an out-of-band update should be along within the next few days to deal with the problem.
According to Microsoft, the technical glitch affects every version of Windows except Windows 11 26H2, stretching back to Windows 10 1809 and LTSC 2019, and Windows Server from 2025 back to 2012.

Microsoft, or rather the unfortunate souls responsible for administering their server products, has not had the best time of late. The October 2026 Windows Server update left some Exchange Servers wobbling until either a Registry edit was made or a fix was applied as part of the November update. ®
cfc6b95240187f97: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — More than a century’s worth of knowledge and information on tropical forest biodiversity and science from the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) is now accessible worldwide through its digital repository, the FRIM Research Depository (FRED).

FRIM said in a statement today that the FRED portal, fully operational since last year, recorded an average of 2,885 user accesses annually and offered free registration for round-the-clock access to 160,244 metadata records and 77,600 digital files.
The digital resources include scientific articles, books, theses, journals, forest maps and newspaper clippings, benefiting researchers, policymakers, industry players, students and the public.
“This digitalisation initiative marks a transformation from the physical services of the FRIM Library in Kepong, which receives an average of 2,200 visitors annually,” the statement said.

Established before 1918 and having survived both British and Japanese administrations, the specialised library houses nearly 200,000 reference materials covering 82 subjects related to forestry and forest products.
FRIM said historical records and documents preserved in the library were also among the key contributors to FRIM’s recognition as a Unesco World Heritage Site.

“To ensure authoritative and systematically organised scientific references, the library’s collection is managed using the Global Forestry Decimal Classification (GFDC), an international hierarchical classification standard also adopted by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the International Union of Forest Research Organisations (IUFRO),” the statement said.

Besides preserving heritage manuscripts from physical deterioration, the library houses four major special collections, namely the Rattan Collection, Bamboo Collection, Asean Collection and FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection.

According to FRIM, the Rattan Collection was developed in 1988 through the Rattan Information Centre (RIC), with funding from the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA), to promote rattan species such as Calamus manan as a scientific commodity and support rural economies.

The Bamboo Collection, established in 1993, contains more than 1,200 reference materials on bamboo research and industry, while the Asean Collection comprises research reports, proceedings on traditional forest management and studies on the regional impact of climate change.
Meanwhile, the FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection serves as the official repository of publications, consultancy reports and conference papers produced by FRIM researchers since 1990.

“Since the establishment of the Forestry School in 1927 and academic collaboration with the Faculty of Forestry at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) beginning in 1971, the FRIM Library has remained a cornerstone of human capital development and forestry education in the country.
“In today’s era of information overload, the FRED portal ensures that the public has access to authentic, reliable and rigorously evaluated scientific references,” the statement said.
Members of the public and the research community can explore the country’s wealth of tropical forest science knowledge through the FRED portal at https://fred.frim.gov.my/Home/Index_v3. — Bernama
e69bc8be8502b3e0: KUALA LUMPUR: Residents of Aman Dua Apartment were left terrified after a foreign man went on a rampage, chasing people and forcing neighbours to lock themselves inside their homes.
Muhammad Aidil Roslan, 26, said he witnessed the incident from his third-floor apartment, which faces the suspect's unit.
The furniture maker, who has lived at the apartment for a year, said the suspect had been behaving unusually in the two weeks leading up to the incident.
"For the past two weeks, he had frequently argued with his housemate. We could hear him shouting and making a lot of noise," he said when met at the apartment.
Aidil said the situation became particularly frightening when the man began chasing anyone who crossed his path.
"When he came towards my house, I immediately went inside and locked the door because I was afraid he would come after me."
He also saw a woman leaving the suspect's unit bleeding, after which the man appeared to be alone.
Aidil said the incident was particularly shocking as the apartment complex had generally been peaceful.
"Seeing what happened to the policemen was frightening and heartbreaking. They were just carrying out their duties, and suddenly something like this happened," he said.
A policeman's hand was severed during the attack.
Another resident, Tan, 58, who has lived at the apartment for more than 25 years, described the suspect as someone who had previously been pleasant and regularly greeted his neighbours.
"He was usually a pleasant man. Whenever we crossed paths, he would greet me. It was only a month ago that his behaviour started changing," he said.
Tan said the suspect's friends had visited the apartment because they were concerned about his behaviour and had contacted the police for help.
He said the man later attacked a police officer with a parang before returning to his unit to change his clothes.
"He then made his way downstairs and began targeting any policeman he saw. He also damaged a police car with the parang he was holding," he said.
Tan said the suspect eventually left the apartment compound and went to a nearby mini-mart before he was shot dead.
Despite the incident, Tan cautioned against blaming the wider foreign community living at the apartment.
He said African nationals made up about five per cent of the residents and had generally lived peacefully alongside locals.
"This was an isolated incident. We should not label all foreigners as bad because of what one person did.
"They are usually unproblematic. I have lived here for more than 25 years, and something like this should not change how we view the entire community," he said.
Aidil also described the incident as the first of its kind he had witnessed at the apartment.
However, he hoped the authorities would strengthen checks on foreigners who misused immigration documents or remained in the country unlawfully.

093490c90d193b48: PETALING JAYA: Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) bersedia memberikan kerjasama penuh kepada pihak berkuasa, termasuk membantu sebarang audit berhubung dakwaan minyak sawit import dicampurkan dengan bekalan tempatan sebelum dieksport semula sebagai produk Malaysia.

31807ad7a719235e: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Turkiye has been selected as the preferred country to supply an alternative to Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the decision was made after the government evaluated proposals from several countries, including Turkiye, France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs.
“We have conducted an evaluation and have now reached the stage of determining that Turkiye is the best country from which to obtain an alternative to our missile.

“We will engage with the Turkish side for further negotiations so that we can finalise the matter,” he told reporters after the Defence Ministry’s 2026 Innovation Day celebration at the Mindef Auditorium today.

He said the government had also received assurances on the missile’s compatibility and integration with the ships’ systems, which would be further examined during negotiations with the Turkish company.

Mohamed Khaled said the missile from Turkiye was of the same type as that already ordered for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project, allowing supplies to be obtained earlier, as early as 2028.
He said the surface-to-surface missile had an operational range of 240 kilometres, with comparable explosive power and greater effectiveness than competing missiles.

In terms of cost, he said Malaysia would not have to bear the full cost of procuring new missiles, as part of the expense had already been absorbed under the LCS contract. Instead, the government would likely only need to cover the cost of installing the launchers and integrating the systems.

“If we did not have the LCS, we would have to order new missiles, which could cost RM700 million, RM800 million or RM900 million. Now, we do not need to spend that amount to replace the NSM,” he said.

On the procurement of the NSM from Norway, Mohamed Khaled said the project had stalled because the Norwegian government had not issued the required licence, meaning Malaysia would not receive the missiles despite having made payment for the procurement.

He said the government was now prepared to take legal action through arbitration, but was bound by several stages of dispute resolution stipulated in the contract, after initial negotiations reached a deadlock.

“We are therefore moving to the second stage, which is to establish a Dispute Resolution Committee between the two parties. If that process fails, Malaysia will proceed to arbitration, which can be held in Kuala Lumpur under the NSM procurement contract,” he said.

Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled said Malaysia was not waiting for the process to be concluded before seeking a replacement for the NSM, to ensure that the country’s defence needs continued to be addressed while the process with Norway was ongoing. — Bernama
ce42f9d09ec39b03: KUALA LUMPUR: Pharmaniaga Bhd's net profit for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) surged 261 per cent to RM26.3 million from RM7.3 million a year earlier, as it recorded RM16.4 million tax benefits.

The group declared a dividend of 0.32 sen per share for the quarter.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M FY26), Pharmaniaga's net profit increased 72.1 per cent to RM70.2 million from RM40.8 million in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue grew 8.2 per cent to RM3.23 billion from RM2.99 billion, primarily driven by stronger demand in its concession segment.

PBT increased 22 per cent to RM77.2 million from RM63.3 million, with the group recording interest savings of RM17.4 million following the partial repayment of borrowings using proceeds from its regularisation plan.
Looking ahead, Pharmaniaga said the government's 2027 budget for healthcare of RM47.7 billion would provide a supportive backdrop for the industry.

The group is also expanding its biopharmaceutical portfolio after securing National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency approval for EVnyx, an Enterovirus 71 vaccine, and ISENDA (liraglutide), its first generic glucagon-like peptide-1 product targeting Type 2 diabetes and weight management.
It plans to launch nine new pharmaceutical products in 2027, focusing on cardiovascular, oncology, anti-infectives and vaccines.
Meanwhile, the group expects the number of products under its Approved Product Purchase List concession to increase from about 850 to more than 1,200 within the concession period.
Pharmaniaga is also progressing with the equipping of four strategically located warehouses, with full operations targeted to commence in the first quarter of 2027.
36f67db3b9e98807: PETALING JAYA: Bekas ketua Pemuda Umno, Khairy Jamaluddin, mencabar menteri daripada DAP supaya meletakkan jawatan sekiranya enggan menghormati titah Yang di-Pertuan Agong berhubung isu pengampunan dan pelaksanaan tahanan di rumah bagi Najib Razak.

Badan Peguam memohon kebenaran untuk mencabar prosiding, keputusan dan tindakan Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan (LPWP) berkaitan aturan tahanan di rumah bertarikh 18 Sept.

Cabaran baharu ini dibuat menjelang keputusan Mahkamah Rayuan pada 7 Jan berhubung rayuan berasingan oleh Badan Peguam terhadap keputusan LPWP pada Januari 2024 yang mengurangkan hukuman penjara dan denda ke atas Najib.
Najib, 73, tiba di kediamannya di Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, kelmarin untuk menjalani baki hukuman penjara enam tahun bagi kes SRC International.
Beliau dipenjarakan di Penjara Kajang sejak 23 Ogos 2022.

Pada Januari 2024, Yang di-Pertuan Agong ketika itu, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah, mengurangkan separuh daripada hukuman penjara 12 tahun ke atas Najib dan mengurangkan denda daripada RM210 juta kepada RM50 juta, melalui pengampunan diraja.

Pada September 2026, Yang di-Pertuan Agong sekarang, Sultan Ibrahim, memberi pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib, membenarkan beliau menjalani baki hukuman di bawah tahanan di rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028.
Denda RM50 juta dibayar oleh Umno menggunakan dana yang dikumpul melalui kaedah pendanaan awam.

1a2d92d1b6f46fe6: PETALING JAYA: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin has urged DAP ministers to quit the Cabinet if they cannot respect the king's decision on Najib Razak's conditional pardon and house arrest.
The former minister questioned whether DAP respected the king only when his decisions were in the party's favour.

Khairy recalled how the then king's intervention helped end the political deadlock after the 2022 general election, allowing the unity government to be formed and Anwar Ibrahim to become prime minister.
“At the time, everyone insisted that the king's decree must be respected. So does respect for the king apply only when his decisions favour us?” he said, according to Berita KS.
Khairy said he was not asking anyone to defend Najib or support his pardon, but political differences should not be a reason to disrespect the king.
"All I ask for is consistency. If we defend the constitution, we must defend it in its entirety. If we respect the constitutional monarchy, we must do so regardless of who benefits from a decision."
Khairy also questioned the Malaysian Bar's move to challenge Najib's house arrest in court, asking who authorised it to act on behalf of the legal profession.
He also took aim at DAP's former Damansara MP Tony Pua, who suggested that questions about Najib's house arrest should be directed to the palace.
Pua had said the king made it clear the decision to grant Najib a pardon was his alone, although the government had given its views.

Khairy, however, pointed to Anwar's statement in the Dewan Rakyat on Dec 10, 2024, when the prime minister said he had personally raised Najib's earlier pardon request at the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting.
The former Rembau MP said this showed that the government did play a role and deserved scrutiny as well.
Najib's house arrest took effect on Tuesday after the High Court issued a fresh order, annulling a previous discharge order given last week.
DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook subsequently stepped down as transport minister.
Loke had announced his resignation in September, saying it was to convey DAP's stand on Najib's conditional pardon.

1f3a0f3cdb160413: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman's commercial crime investigation department (CCID) will send a team of officers to Pakistan soon to obtain further information regarding the detention of 130 Malaysians in Rawalpindi last month.

He said examining the evidence was very important to uncover the syndicate's modus operandi, including the use of Malaysian police uniforms to deceive victims.
"We need to arrange a meeting to obtain statements from the authorities there, in addition to examining the evidence or devices seized.

He said the identities of the Malaysians were confirmed through cooperation among the police, embassies and Interpol.
He said 59 were from Sabah, 57 from Sarawak, and the rest from Johor, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Kelantan.
"Checks found that 92 of them do not have criminal records in Malaysia. The others have records for various offences including drugs, fraud and gambling.
"Two of them are wanted by the police in connection with fraud cases in Sabah."
He added that 107 of them had overstayed their visas in Pakistan, while 20 had valid visas, two had visa extensions, and one did not have valid travel documents.

986fe7d205dc3b07: European tech buyers are increasingly choosing cybersecurity vendors from their own continent in a bid to reduce their reliance on American technology.
Digital sovereignty isn't only prompting enterprise customers to question their clouds of choice, it is also reshaping other parts of the industry too, and the shift is marked.

According to sales figures compiled by Context, distributor sales in EMEA of cybersecurity products from EU-headquartered vendors jumped 35 percent in the two years to calendar Q3 2026. Total cybersecurity sales grew up 10 percent over the same period, and sales by US-run companies went up just 8 percent.

That growth is from a relatively small base, though EU vendors gained nearly three percentage points to reach 15 percent of tracked sales by value. There is still a long way to go as US-headquartered vendors accounted for 62 percent.

The trend coincides with a loss of trust in the Trump administration among customers outside of America, after it cosied up to autocratic rulers while criticizing and punishing allies with tariffs and more.

Context stopped short of assigning blame. It said organizations are reviewing their reliance on third-party tech in light of EU compliance regimes: the NIS2 Directive and Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

NIS2, transposed into national law in October 2024, requires organizations in the bloc to raise their common level of security in the face of digital threats and risks to critical infrastructure. DORA, introduced in January last year, is designed to strengthen cyber security in the financial sector.

"Digital sovereignty is becoming a buying decision. As customers and resellers get clearer about what it means in practice, they're asking who holds the encryption keys, who can access sensitive logs and where that data is stored," said Context veep of research Joe Turner.

"We're seeing a measurable shift in the EMEA channel. EU vendors gained nearly three points of sales share in two years. An organization can keep its existing identity platform and still choose a European supplier to manage its security logs. That's the kind of decision that gives European vendors an opening."

The stats indicate that EU-HQd vendors comprised 92 percent of tracked sales in security awareness training, 82 percent in vulnerability management, and 52 percent for SIEM and log management. US-headquartered companies held into 74 percent of identity and access management sales and 54 percent of cloud security sales.

The Reg has asked Context for UK-specific figures to see whether British customers are also voting with their wallets for European alternatives. That certainly isn’t the case for tech purchases in the British public sector, despite Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s professed desire to buy British.
Data released yesterday by the Institute for Public Policy Research showed just £1 in every £6 spent by government with the biggest technology suppliers goes to Brit businesses.
Still, Burnham only came to power in July so there is time yet for him to put his money where his mouth is.

Sovereign AI is another area of concern for enterprise customers. Analyst Omdia said last month that despite the marketing adjective meaning "local assets," almost a third AI providers disclose no proof of sovereignty, and some "expect enterprise to pay for audits to verify their claims."

Omdia also found that 80 percent of contracts say network resilience is "out of providers control or responsibility," and "US-headquartered AI providers offer better service transparency and contract terms than a majority of local sovereign AI providers, with providers in India a notable exception."
Sovereign services in Omdia's classification include data residency, operational autonomy, jurisdictional sovereignty, and technological autonomy.

"Local hosting is not sovereignty. Serious providers must demonstrate their credibility through transparent operations, fair contracts and proof of competence. That includes the network, because data in transit must be sovereign too," said Camille Mendler, research director for telco B2B at Omdia.
Someone should tell Microsoft and Anthropic. ®

f4dfe2a6d2564dc5: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) is prepared to introduce regulations under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 to enable consumers to check the sources of slaughterhouses and the halal certification status of chicken sold in the market.

Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the move was among efforts to strengthen protection for Muslim consumers following concerns raised by members of parliament over the monitoring and transparency of the halal status of chicken supplies.

He said KPDN also agreed with a proposal by Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) that responsibility for ensuring the integrity of the halal supply chain should not rest solely with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and state religious authorities, but should also involve KPDN in enforcement and local authorities (PBT) in monitoring business premises.

“Therefore, KPDN will propose better coordination with state religious authorities, local authorities and the Health Ministry to improve the monitoring of slaughterhouses and chicken sales premises,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates at the committee stage for the ministry.

On the proposal to restrict eligibility for purchasing packet cooking oil to recipients of the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance, Armizan said it was a good suggestion, but its implementation would need to be phased in to avoid affecting small traders, including night market vendors.
He said the government first needed to stabilise the implementation of targeted diesel and petrol subsidies before considering more comprehensive reforms to subsidies for other essential goods.

On the Electronic Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme (eCOSS), Armizan said the system enabled the government to obtain more comprehensive data on the supply, sale and purchase of packet cooking oil, helping it determine quota reductions and better target subsidies based on actual data.

“eCOSS was introduced in May 2023 to monitor the distribution of subsidised packet cooking oil from repackagers to wholesalers and retailers. This was followed by the Mobile eCOSS application, which records consumers’ purchase details through QR code scanning,” he said.

Earlier, during the debate, several MPs raised concerns about enforcement at chicken slaughterhouses whose halal status was in doubt, following a recent raid on a slaughterhouse in Puchong that led to the seizure of 6.5 tonnes of raw chickens and the arrest of 12 foreign workers.

Among them was Idris, who stressed that the issue should not be viewed from a political perspective but treated seriously, as it could undermine consumer confidence in the halal status of food products in the country.

Meanwhile, Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) proposed that the ministry consider issuing Budi Madani petrol and diesel sales permits to selected grocery shops in remote areas, as well as providing MyKad verification terminals to allow eligible residents to access subsidies without compromising efforts to prevent leakages.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved KPDN’s 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates totalling RM2,366,037,400, with a majority vote after 17 MPs took part in the debate. — Bernama
108bdd7b842066b7: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's system for tracking subsidised cooking oil cannot identify buyers, leaving gaps that allow leakages and misuse, Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said.
He said the electronic Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme (eCOSS), introduced in May 2023, could track supplies delivered to retailers but not identify buyers.
"We know how much is supplied and the quota reaching retailers, but we do not have data on who buys the cooking oil," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Armizan was winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for his ministry.
He said some retailers had allegedly stored subsidised cooking oil packets before selling them in bulk to certain parties.
Others had reportedly opened the packets and transferred the contents into bottles for resale at higher prices.
To address the gaps, Armizan said the ministry had introduced the Mobile eCOSS application, which requires consumers to scan a QR code when buying subsidised cooking oil packets.
He said the system would help authorities identify buyers, monitor purchases and improve subsidy targeting.
Although the requirement had drawn complaints from consumers, Armizan said the data was necessary to curb leakages.
"Leakages are still occurring. I do not deny that, but compared with before, there has been a reduction," he said.
Armizan said enforcement had also been strengthened, while the ministry had revised the distribution system to improve access to subsidised cooking oil.

Under the new arrangement, repackaging companies determine 50 per cent of distribution destinations, while the ministry's state and district offices decide where the remaining supplies should be delivered.
c2bc5d927c16e204: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Plantations Group Bhd (JPG) reported a net profit of RM100.32 million for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), representing a 5.45 per cent decline from RM106.04 million in the corresponding quarter last year.

Despite the year-on-year moderation, the group demonstrated a robust sequential recovery, with net profit surging 96 per cent quarter-on-quarter from the RM51.2 million posted in the immediate preceding quarter.

According to the group's financial statements, revenue for Q3 FY26 stood at RM450.72 million, a 9.2 per cent contraction from RM496.15 million a year ago. However, against the preceding quarter, revenue grew by 8.4 per cent from RM415.84 million.
The revenue decline was largely attributed to lower delivery volumes, with crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel (PK) deliveries falling by 15.9 per cent and 10.4 per cent, respectively.

This drop in volume was partially offset by stronger selling prices, with the average CPO selling price 6.5 per cent higher in Q3 FY26 at RM4,683 per tonne, compared with in Q3 FY25. Similarly, the average PK selling price rose by 6.6 per cent to RM3,747 per tonne.
The group faced rising operational expenses during the quarter, with internal CPO cost of production increasing by 13.5 per cent from a year ago, to RM2,526 per tonne.

However, the impressive quarterly profit rebound was heavily driven by a 35.6 per cent surge in fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production, which reached 292,352 tonnes in line with the seasonal peak crop cycle.
This higher output allowed fixed costs to be spread over a larger volume, effectively lowering the internal CPO cost of production by 9.4 per cent sequentially from RM2,788 per tonne.

For the cumulative nine-month period, JPG's net profit contracted by 21.3 per cent to RM201.93 million, driven by higher production and operating costs, alongside lower finance income. Its revenue slipped 0.9 per cent during the period to RM1.22 billion.

The board of directors approved and declared a third interim single-tier dividend of 1.50 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026. The dividend, totaling approximately RM37.38 million, will be payable on Dec 10.
Looking ahead to the final quarter of 2026, JPG anticipates CPO prices to remain broadly range-bound.
The group noted that while biodiesel demand and seasonal consumption will provide support, elevated inventory levels may constrain significant price upside.
"Prolonged dry conditions and the potential lagged effects of El Niño on yields remain key uncertainties affecting the production outlook," said JPG.
Indonesia's B50 biodiesel programme remains a structural demand driver, though its impact will depend on domestic production and consumption trends.
The group also acknowledged impending cost pressures from the higher minimum wage, which is expected to increase labour costs across the plantation sector.

In response, JPG remains focused on improving productivity, accelerating mechanisation, and maintaining strict cost discipline to mitigate these pressures while advancing its strategic growth initiatives.

e13c367e91f024b2: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — It hasn’t been a month since the iPhone Duo’s launch on October 23, and what was once a weakness (lack of app support) is swiftly being remedied.

For instance: In Malaysia, popular local coffee chain Zus has already added iPhone Duo support to its app, cleverly incorporating the front display and optimising the app’s layout on the inner foldout screen.
DuoBook allows easy pairing of the iPhone Duo to a nearby Mac, turning the phone into a mini MacBook.
Readgio turns your iPhone Duo into a book, allowing you to easily read PDFs or e-books and turning the outer iPhone Duo display into a book cover.
The viral Deck-Man brings back retro nostalgia by converting the phone into a miniature portable cassette recorder.
These are just a few examples from an increasingly growing list of new apps or apps adding support for Apple’s first foldable.
On the response to the phone, Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, said in a statement:

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation. Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimised apps are being added to the store each day.

“In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users. 4fc829def6124b99: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has praised the Malaysian Indian Muslim Congress (Kimma) for its unwavering loyalty, crediting the party for consistently supporting Umno and BN over several decades of elections.
The Umno president said Kimma had stood by the party for more than 30 years as a trusted ally, making it an important part of BN's support base.
Founded in 1976 to champion the socioeconomic and political interests of Malaysia's Indian Muslim community, Kimma has long sought full component party membership in BN.
Although it remains outside BN's formal Supreme Council structure, it was granted associate member status with Umno in 2010.

"In every by-election and state election campaign, Kimma has shown its own resolve and worked tirelessly to gather Indian Muslim voters to support BN candidates," Zahid said at a gathering hosted by Kimma in Pengkalan Batu.
"I see that Indian Muslim voters in Melaka remain deeply loyal and steadfast with BN," he added, while thanking KIMMA president Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Kader for his leadership in mobilising support.

Zahid also called on the community to extend its support to Perikatan Nasional candidates, including PN candidate for Ayer Keroh Michael Gan, under the electoral pact between the two coalitions, with BN contesting 23 seats and PN five.

Kimma president Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Kader said the party had activated its grassroots machinery across all 28 constituencies in Melaka, including setting up a dedicated call centre, to ensure the state's estimated 2,850 Indian Muslim voters turned out on polling day.
"Through our Jalinan Rakyat network, we have already compiled voter data and met with them even before candidate nominations," he said.

"On Nov 14, our call centre will contact voters to remind them to cast their ballots and assist those who need transport or face any issues. Our task is to ensure every Indian Muslim voter is brought out to vote."
Syed Ibrahim added that supporting BN was a strict party directive, warning that members who failed to support the coalition risked being expelled.
Indian Muslims account for about three per cent of Melaka's electorate.
767b7ee02e5ca0de: LONDON: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign, with US boss Mauricio Pochettino widely expected to replace him.

Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone.
"Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men's first-team head coach," the club said in a statement.

"Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.
"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions."
Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away.
But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions.
It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.
Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January.
But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, the team have endured a steep decline this season.
Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como.
And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings.
Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain.
The Argentine signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago.

But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach.

Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago, with United yet to win a Premier League title since the retirement of the outstanding Scottish manager.
The Red Devils, once the dominant force in English football, have been overtaken by Manchester City, Liverpool and Arsenal.
United's next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Nov 22. - AFP
713a71cb54e7323d: PETALING JAYA: Penang police have arrested four Pakistani nationals, including two women, to assist in investigations into a robbery in which a 43-year-old policeman was injured by suspects armed with sharp objects near a petrol station in Permatang Pauh, Penang, on Tuesday.

eb98bffd00314f04: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim chaired a special meeting at Parliament House today to streamline coordination in tackling recurring floods in Selangor.

Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting focused on four key actions, beginning with strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving disaster management coordination through the Selangor State Disaster Management Committee.
The other two measures involve resolving flash floods through the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) and studying Kuala Lumpur City Hall's (DBKL) flood management best practices.
"Special attention is being given to flood-prone areas, particularly in the Petaling and Kuala Selangor districts, which recorded 1,180 evacuees at seven temporary relief centres as of Nov 12, 2026.

dcae38e475a3e452: GEORGE TOWN: Pulau Pinang boleh menarik diri daripada perjanjian bernilai RM24.6 bilion untuk membeli air terawat dari Perak tanpa perlu membayar pampasan, sekiranya caj yang dipersetujui tidak diluluskan oleh pengawal selia persekutuan, kata Ketua Menteri Chow Kon Yeow.
Beliau berkata perjanjian selama 40 tahun itu tertakluk kepada kelulusan caj yang dipersetujui oleh Suruhanjaya Perkhidmatan Air Negara (SPAN).

Chow memberikan jaminan itu selepas lima pengarah bebas di syarikat air, PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB), membangkitkan kebimbangan berhubung bayaran yang mungkin masih perlu dilunaskan sekiranya bekalan air dari Perak terganggu.

Chow berkata pembekal air Perak, iaitu usaha sama antara Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Perak dan Gamuda Bhd (PKNPk-Gamuda JV), mempunyai tempoh sehingga 2035 untuk mendapatkan kelulusan SPAN bagi caj berkenaan.
"Jika mereka tidak dapat mencapainya, kita boleh kata kita akan menarik diri," katanya selepas mesyuarat agung luar biasa (EGM) PBAHB.
PBAHB memaklumkan bahawa 97.9% undi yang dibuat pada mesyuarat yang dihadiri oleh 161 pemegang saham itu bersetuju dengan perjanjian tersebut.
Undian itu memenuhi salah satu daripada dua syarat yang diperlukan untuk perjanjian tersebut diteruskan. Satu lagi syarat adalah kelulusan SPAN terhadap caj yang dipersetujui.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PBAHB, K Pathmanathan, berkata PBAHB tidak perlu membayar pampasan sekiranya kelulusan tidak diperoleh. Katanya lagi, PKNPk-Gamuda JV akan menanggung kos pembinaan loji rawatan air.
Lima pengarah berkenaan sebelum ini membangkitkan kebimbangan mengenai obligasi kewangan PBAHB sekiranya bekalan air terputus selepas perjanjian itu berkuat kuasa.
Chow mengambil maklum kebimbangan mereka, dan berkata lembaga pengarah mengambil masa kira-kira setahun untuk membincangkan terma-terma perjanjian.

Pulau Pinang dijangka mula menerima bekalan air dari Perak pada 31 Mac 2032, dengan pilihan untuk meningkatkan pembelian sehingga 500 juta liter sehari bagi mengelakkan kekurangan bekalan pada masa hadapan seiring pertumbuhan penduduk dan industri.

Menurut perjanjian itu, Pulau Pinang perlu membayar caj kapasiti tahunan sebanyak RM210 juta bagi memastikan kemudahan rawatan air di Perak terus beroperasi, selain caj air terawat sebanyak RM1.70 bagi setiap meter padu (1,000 liter), tertakluk kepada semakan setiap tiga tahun.

Ini bermakna Pulau Pinang akan membayar kira-kira RM396 juta setahun walaupun hanya membeli kuantiti minimum sebanyak 300 juta liter sehari. Perjanjian itu dijangka menelan kos sebanyak RM24.6 bilion sepanjang tempoh 40 tahun, merangkumi pembelian air dan caj tetap bagi kapasiti rawatan.
PBAHB juga dijangka membelanjakan kira-kira RM400 juta untuk saluran paip dan kemudahan lain bagi mengagihkan air ke seluruh Pulau Pinang.

Pulau Pinang kini memperoleh kira-kira 80% air mentahnya dari Sungai Muda, yang dikongsi bersama Kedah, sekali gus menjadikannya terdedah kepada kekurangan bekalan semasa musim kemarau yang berpanjangan.

9ec9a8e150cb297d: KUALA LUMPUR: A backbencher has asked the home ministry to arrange an official visit by members of the special select committee on security to Najib Razak’s residence, which has been gazetted as a prison for his house arrest.
Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong), a member of the committee, said the visit was to ensure the house arrest arrangements complied with stipulated procedures and safety requirements.
"If everything is in order, there is no reason to fear an inspection by Parliament,” he said today while debating the 2027 budget at the committee stage for the home ministry.

Lim's suggestion comes after home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the security arrangements would incur no additional cost to the government, as personnel had been reassigned from their existing duties at Kajang prison to Najib's home.

Saifuddin said the conditions for the former prime minister’s house arrest cover restrictions on his residence, association, movement, visits and the use of telecommunication devices. They also include mandatory participation in rehabilitation and intervention programmes.
He also said prisons department officers were stationed at the residence in three shifts, with three officers working each shift, alongside a continuous police presence.
However, Lim asked who would replace these officers at Kajang prison.
“Also, what are the travel costs and allowances, and how much does it cost to assign police personnel? What is the impact on normal prison operations?” the DAP MP asked.

Najib, 73, arrived at his home in Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, on Tuesday night to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence in the SRC International case, having previously been in Kajang prison since Aug 23, 2022.
In January 2024, the then Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah, halved Najib's 12-year prison sentence and reduced his RM210 million fine to RM50 million under a royal pardon.

In September 2026, the current Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

5c52ec467afa733a: BANGI, Nov 12 — A total of 143 positions have been approved for the establishment of the Public Defender’s Office, with appointments to be made as soon as possible to strengthen access to legal aid services in the country.

The office would be headed by an officer at the JUSA C level, with approval for the establishment of the posts already obtained from the Finance Ministry, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

“This marks a new chapter for the Legal Aid Department (JBG). As we discussed during the debate on amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, we looked at the roles the government should play alongside the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), as a substantial amount of government funding goes directly to YBGK.

“Now, we will establish the Public Defender’s Office to work alongside YBGK,” she told reporters after the presentation of certificates for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and appointments of mediators, as well as the launch of the Legal Aid Department’s Madani Mediation Centre Handbook 2026, here today.

Azalina said the Public Defender’s Office was part of the government’s efforts to modernise the legal aid system, moving beyond the traditional approach to provide services that better meet the needs of the public.
She said the amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, which were passed by Parliament in August last year, were expected to come into force in the first quarter of 2027.
“What is most important to me is that the public defender works closely with the existing YBGK unit, while continuing to cooperate with the Bar Council and State Bar Committees,” she said.
Meanwhile, Azalina said the government hoped to make mediation part of everyday practice among Malaysians through the establishment of the Madani Mediation Centre (PMM).
She said the initiative would complement the existing legal aid services provided by JBG under the Legal Aid Act by offering another avenue for alternative dispute resolution.
“With mediation, people can come to JBG to seek an alternative dispute resolution platform through the mediation services offered under PMM.
“This is a more people-centric approach as it gives parties in a dispute the opportunity to resolve their differences through mediation,” she said.

At the event, 210 participants completed six series of the Professional Mediation Certification Course organised by JBG in collaboration with Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia and the National Legal Training Institute.
The programme was funded through an allocation of RM680,000 under the 2026 Budget Initiative to strengthen mediation expertise in the public sector.

Azalina also launched the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, developed by JBG as a key reference to ensure that case-handling procedures, professional ethics and mediation service standards are implemented systematically and consistently nationwide. — Bernama

94cbf139538e3243: More than 1,600 Rockstar Games employees in the UK will begin voting on union recognition on Thursday, with the ballot kicking off just a week before the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.

The ballot, which opens on November 12 and runs until November 26, will determine whether Rockstar formally recognizes the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote.
If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice.

The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI.

The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, although the people responsible for making it have rather more immediate concerns than sales records.

"I am incredibly proud of the work we've put into making this game. I'm also proud of the union we've built here. For me, those two things are connected," said Nestor Uriate, an animation programmer and Rockstar Game Workers Union representative.

"We care deeply about the games we make, and we want to make sure we can continue doing that work in an environment where we're respected, have a meaningful say over our conditions and can feel secure about our futures."

The vote follows a year of bad blood between Rockstar and the IWGB. The union accused the GTA developer of union busting after it fired 31 members in October 2025, claiming they had been singled out for taking part in a private Discord group.
Rockstar denied the allegations, insisting the workers were dismissed for gross misconduct rather than their union activities.

The dispute subsequently reached an employment tribunal, where Rockstar unsuccessfully attempted to have blacklisting allegations struck from the case. Closing submissions are expected on November 17 and 18, meaning the legal proceedings will reach their final stages just as GTA VI prepares to hit shelves.

Despite the ongoing dispute, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, recently indicated that management would respect the outcome of the recognition vote, telling Bloomberg: "We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union."
The union campaign has also attracted support from elsewhere in the games industry, including SAG-AFTRA and the Communications Workers of America (CWA), which represents workers at Blizzard.
Alex Marshall, president of the IWGB, said the vote was an opportunity for Rockstar employees to take greater control over their working conditions.

"What happens at Rockstar matters beyond the studio. Workers across the games industry are watching, and this ballot is an opportunity to show what can be achieved when people come together, organize and build the collective power to shape their own working lives."

For Rockstar, November was already shaping up to be a big month. By the time GTA VI has been in players' hands for a week, the company should also know whether its UK workforce has voted to secure a formal seat at the negotiating table. ®
