4ddcddee04759d96: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Madani government is committed to gradually reducing the fiscal deficit from 5.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022 to 3.3 per cent in 2027.

Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the reduction in the fiscal deficit reflects the government’s commitment to strengthen the country’s financial position, thereby helping to lower the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP.

He said the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP, which was 65.2 per cent at the end of 2025, was projected to decrease to 64 per cent at the end of this year and further to 63.7 per cent in 2027.
“This is part of the government’s efforts to carry out fiscal reforms to ensure that the level of debt is at the appropriate level,” he told reporters at Deloitte’s 52nd TaxMax conference here today.

He said the fiscal expansion policy in Budget 2027 is key to supporting economic growth, keeping the unemployment rate low, and increasing people’s income to help households deal with the cost-of-living challenge.

Commenting on the proposed re-implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), he said the move may not be appropriate at this time, given economic uncertainty and the government’s priority to increase people’s income amid the cost-of-living challenge.
He said the government still prioritises efforts to increase people’s income, including through a minimum wage increase.

Johan said the proposal to replace the Sales and Service Tax (SST) with GST at an equivalent rate would not necessarily increase government revenue, but rather potentially shift part of the tax burden from the business sector, including exporters, to consumers.
“The Prime Minister has commented on the issue of GST and SST several times. Although GST may have its advantages, it may not be the right time at this juncture.
“There may also be some misunderstandings or misinterpretations, which are not accurate, with some parties suggesting to implement GST to increase revenue.
He said that those who propose introducing GST to increase the country’s revenue may need a higher GST rate, and that is not something the government wants at this time.
To date, Johan said SST collections stand at 3.2 per cent of GDP, the same ratio as GST collections in 2017. — Bernama

a1c98e67407a0d4d: MADRID: More than 3 million Spaniards took to the streets on Wednesday as part of a mostly peaceful general strike protesting against a growing housing crisis, unions said, though 115 people were arrested, mainly during evening clashes in Barcelona and Madrid.
Workers endured stormy weather to set up picket lines, with large marches in Madrid, Barcelona and other cities across Spain less than three weeks before a snap general election.
In the evening, clashes between police and some protesters erupted in Barcelona. Furniture was set alight in the street after the main march ended, Reuters video showed.
Tensions also rose in Madrid, when riot police used foam bullets, tear gas and pepper spray to disperse protesters around the central Plaza de Espana, a Reuters witness said.
Police forces reported at least 115 arrests nationwide from incidents linked to the general strike, including blockades of offices and industrial estates.

Sumar, the Socialist government's junior coalition partner, called on Thursday for interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska to resign over what it described as an "excessive and disproportionate" response by police.
Amnesty International said it had documented excessive use of police force including blows with batons on peaceful protesters and indiscriminate use of pepper spray on crowds.
Grande-Marlaska on Thursday ordered investigations into the incidents, the Interior Ministry said.

It was the first general strike since workers downed tools in 2012 against austerity measures during the euro zone debt crisis. The Tenants Union said more than 3 million people, including unionised workers as well as students, pensioners, tenants, the self-employed and jobless, took part in demonstrations to protest against rising rents and evictions.
A strike by Spanish women in 2018 drew 5 million people, according to unions.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez hopes to harness voter resentment over housing in the Nov 29 election to shift the attention away from a deadly migration rush into Ceuta and a train crash last month. His government has defended its handling of the disasters but so far, his Socialist Party still trails in opinion polls.
Unions described the strike as a success even though participation was uneven across Spain, with the strongest support in coastal regions where housing pressures have been particularly acute.
Shops shuttered
On Madrid's Gran Via, one of the capital's main shopping streets, protesters cheered as stores including Primark, H&M and Pull&Bear brought down their shutters amid a heavy riot police presence.
"We're going to close the Mango store," the protesters chanted as they jangled sets of house keys above their heads.
Spain has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to more than a million by 2028, according to the central bank.

With fewer people able to afford a home, renting has increased sharply, putting pressure on that market. The average rental price of €1,176 is equivalent to about 98.7% of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.

"I’m 36 years old and I still can’t move out on my own," said Madrid resident Jesus Gonzalez, who works in a hospital IT department and supports the strike. "Rents just keep going up, house prices just keep going up, and it’s simply impossible."
Strong turnout at ports, auto plants

Angela de Miguel, vice-president of Spain's main business lobby CEOE, said the strike was counterproductive because small businesses were also affected by the housing crisis, since shortages of homes made recruitment more challenging.
Speaking on state broadcaster TVE, she said the solution was to build more homes and to lower taxes on construction and the home-buying process.

Two heavy storms, dubbed Charles and Bruna, threatened plans for massive protest marches in the afternoon, with unions suspending demonstrations in the southern port city of Cadiz and other cities in the south.

According to UGT and CCOO, participation in the strike reached 90% at ports and in the automotive sector, with "total stoppages" reported at factories including Volkswagen's in Navarre and SEAT's in Barcelona.
Less impact due to remote work
Barcelona's metro said no trains would run outside peak commuting hours, while Madrid's metro said peak-hour usage was down 42% compared with the same period last week.

However, with more people able to work remotely and the increasing weight of services in Spain’s economy, the impact of the strike is likely to be less pronounced than in previous years, according to Miguel Cardoso, chief economist at BBVA Research. He estimated that the strike could shave 0.1% to 0.2% off Spain’s annual gross domestic product.
Spain's fast-growing hospitality and finance industries are less unionised than the public and industrial sectors.

Unions said they would file a criminal complaint against what they described as a “disproportionate” response during a police operation involving tear gas and batons that injured 20 protesters. The interior ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The strike follows weeks of demonstrations provoked by the eviction and subsequent death of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid.
Those protests, along with parliament's rejection last month of government decrees aimed at curbing evictions and limiting rent pressures, prompted Sanchez to call the snap election.

aef96f565dadc3bc: GEORGE TOWN: Penang can walk away from its RM24.6 billion deal to buy treated water from Perak without paying compensation if the agreed charges are not approved by federal regulators, says chief minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the 40-year agreement was still subject to approval of the agreed charges by the National Water Services Commission (SPAN).

His assurance comes after five independent directors of PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB), Penang’s Bursa-listed water company, raised concerns over payments that could still be due if water supplies from Perak were disrupted.
Chow said Perak's water supplier, a joint venture between Perak State Development Corporation and Gamuda Bhd (PKNPk-Gamuda JV), has until 2035 to secure SPAN's approval for the charges.
“If they cannot achieve that, we can say that we will walk away,” he said after PBAHB’s extraordinary general meeting today.
In a handout, PBAHB said 97.9% of the votes cast at the meeting, attended by 161 shareholders, were in favour of the deal.
The vote fulfils one of two conditions needed for the agreement to proceed, the other being SPAN's approval of the agreed charges.
PBAHB CEO K Pathmanathan said the company would not have to pay compensation if approval was not obtained, adding that PKNPk-Gamuda JV would bear the cost of building the water treatment plant.
The five directors had raised concerns about PBAHB's financial obligations if water supplies were interrupted after the agreement took effect.
Chow said he acknowledged their concerns, adding that the board had spent about a year discussing the agreement's terms.

Penang is expected to begin receiving water from Perak on March 31, 2032, with the option to increase purchases to 500 million litres daily to prevent future shortages as Penang's population and industries grow.

Under the deal, the state must pay an annual capacity charge of RM210 million to keep the Perak water treatment facilities running, in addition to a treated water charge of RM1.70 per cubic metre (1,000 litres), subject to review every three years.

This means Penang will pay about RM396 million a year even if it buys only the minimum 300 million litres a day. The deal is expected to cost RM24.6 billion over 40 years, covering both water purchases and fixed charges for treatment capacity.
PBAHB is also expected to spend about RM400 million on pipelines and other facilities to distribute the water within Penang.
The state currently gets about 80% of its raw water from Sungai Muda, which it shares with Kedah, making it vulnerable to shortages during prolonged dry spells.

61db3e7f4b69ca0f: SIBU, Nov 12 — Native Customary Rights (NCR) land ownership in Sarawak continues to be protected through land surveys conducted only upon the application and consent of stakeholders to prevent boundary disputes, encroachment and the loss of rights to ancestral land.

Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan said every survey application must undergo scrutiny and verification of ownership evidence by the Sarawak Land and Survey Department to ensure the claims are legally valid.
He stressed that the state government would not conduct land surveys arbitrarily without first engaging with and obtaining the consent of landowners or claimants.
“We have stipulated that surveys must be carried out upon application. Before any survey work begins, we hold engagement sessions and discussions with stakeholders.

“We want to avoid misunderstandings or allegations that the government is attempting to seize people’s land,” he said at the presentation ceremony for Native Communal Reserve gazette notifications, land titles and land compensation cheques for Sibu Division here today.
Awang Tengah said NCR land surveys would not be carried out on land subject to unresolved ownership disputes or pending court cases until the matters had been settled.

He said that since the introduction of the new NCR land survey initiative in 2010 until October 31 this year, a total of 1,248,659 hectares had undergone perimeter surveys, of which 979,434 hectares had been gazetted as Native Communal Reserves.
During the same period, 112,717 individual lots covering 135,332 hectares had been surveyed, while land titles had been issued for 40,796 lots covering 60,727 hectares.
At the ceremony, 167 land titles were presented to 158 recipients, while five areas covering 21,942.13 hectares in Sibu and Kanowit were gazetted as Native Communal Reserves.
The state government also distributed RM12.69 million in land compensation to 165 recipients affected by five development projects in Sibu Division. — Bernama
37248e32a1da39b1: A new extension brings a working global menu bar to the GNOME desktop, even for some apps that don’t have menu bars at all.

Orbit Global Menu is a new GNOME extension that gives the GNOME desktop a feature it was intentionally designed without, and one that some users miss very badly – this vulture being one of them. It adds a working global menu bar to the GNOME top panel. We suspect this is something that will cause strongly contrasting opinions among many GNOME users: some will by puzzled why anyone would bother, while others may think "at last!" and rush to try it.

There have been other attempts to do this before, and the Reg FOSS desk has tried several of them, but we never found one that worked with the majority of applications. Our fondness for this UI feature was visible in the two-part series we wrote in September on how to customize Xfce and then in part two how to get the global menu working with more apps.

The problem is getting worse over time, as in recent versions (since GNOME 40 and Gtk4), the GNOME human-interface guidelines encourage smartphone-style hamburger menus, replacing the traditional horizontal menu bar. It is tricky to add global menu bar support to apps that lack a menu bar, but Orbit's developer "Unmade" found a rather labor-intensive solution. The menu bar applet contains maps of keyboard controls for 292 different apps, so it can show a menu all on its own and then send those apps simulated keystrokes to operate it. It's not the programs' full menu trees, just a subset of them, but it works.

It's also not the most elegant solution, but it is a solution and it works. We tried it on Ubuntu 26.10 and every app in the full install worked to at least some extent. If you are willing and able to build and install a small additional connector, it lets the global-menu applet talk to lots more applications.

The GNOME shell is unusual among open source desktop environments, to an extent that we have criticized before. GNOME Shell was designed with a distinctive look and feel of its own, unlike almost all other desktops. It has a minimalist, stripped-down layout that doesn't look or work quite like anything else, and it's intentionally not very customizable. To change how GNOME works means writing new Javascript code, then packaging it as an extension that users can install from the GNOME Extensions website. This requires both a browser extension and a "native host messaging" connector to be installed into the underlying OS – or a purpose-written app. By default, the desktop comes with neither.

The end result is that GNOME lends a visual identity to the Linux desktop, one that is clear and distinct from either Windows or macOS. (Back in 2013, this vulture argued that when Microsoft threatened to sue multiple Linux vendors over infringing Windows UI patents, some 20 years ago, this UI fragmentation was just what the company wanted.) GNOME 2 was the Linux world's default desktop. GNOME Shell was controversial in its early days, and lost pole position, but it has since won it back. Today, GNOME is the default desktop on all the major distros: Ubuntu, Fedora and Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the RHELatives, as well as Debian and SUSE, all default to GNOME.

GNOME does away with a lot of features that are significant functional parts of other graphical desktops. For instance, it has no desktop icons, no system tray or defined place for status indicators, and neither GNOME nor GNOME-compliant applications have menu bars, either inside windows (Microsoft style) or in the top panel (Apple macOS style). This is disorienting and confusing for those used to controlling software mainly using their menus – but now, that's mainly older hands. This design suits those who grew up on smartphones and tablets, or who feel more comfortable with their stripped-back keyboardless UI than a full desktop WIMP, which can be overwhelming to newbies and non-techies.

If you've followed the evolution of graphical desktops for some 40 years, as this gray-plumed vulture has, some trends are very apparent that aren't so clear if you came in once evolution was underway.

Apple introduced the first global menu bar in the Lisa, and improved on that in the Macintosh. DR GEM copied it very early on, but Apple sued and DR changed the PC version of GEM to be less Mac-like. Microsoft's Windows came along after this, and moved menu bars inside windows instead. When Apple acquired NeXT in 1996, it moved NeXTstep's patent-avoidant vertical menus back to a global bar at the top, along with the clock and some status indicators. There they remain, 30 years later. In 2007, it launched the iPhone, containing a very cut-down OS based on OS X, replacing the Finder with a cut-down version of the Dashboard layer from OS X 10.4. The panel remained, shorn of its menus, which were too fiddly for a small screen.

As The Register mentioned in 2017, in its preliminary releases, Android started out as a keypad-driven Java phone that looked and worked very much like BlackBerry. When the iPhone appeared, Google changed course. The new Android UI resembled iOS, complete with that top panel, still without menus. GNOME 3.0 was not far behind: in 2009 the team promised a revamp of the user experience, and in 2011, launched GNOME 3.0. It too has the fixed top panel — now huge on a laptop or desktop landscape screen – and mostly empty.

Now that top panel regains its original 1983 function. We're rather impressed by the Orbit global menu. It does the job, and it even works with apps that don't have menu bars. It's not perfect: for instance, over-long menus have to scroll, and may fail to do so if new submenus appear.

The GitHub repository has extensive instructions, including how to build and install the optional connector module that lets more apps export their real menus to the extension. It also tells you how to instruct some apps, notably Firefox, that there is a global menu for it to use. We are saddened to note that, as is so often the case, Wayland gets in the way here.

It works rather well with some other extensions, too. With a menu bar, GNOME's strangely centered clock seems out of place, but several extensions, such as Frippery Move Clock, shove it over to the right where we still feel it belongs. If you prefer a lighter-colored panel and dock, it also plays nicely with Blur my Shell. ®

e65da93452259395: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — The Penang government will hold engagement sessions to explore the possibility of raising the minimum age for Muslims to marry to 18, following similar moves by Selangor and Kedah.

Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Mohamad Abdul Hamid, who is also Penang Islamic Religious Council (MAINPP) president, said the sessions would be held to gather views and assess whether the proposed change could be implemented in the state.
“So far, no discussions have been held on the proposal. We may first organise engagement sessions to explore whether it can be implemented in Penang.
“The sessions will also involve the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry before any decision is made or further developments are announced,” he told reporters here today.

Mohamad was speaking after witnessing the signing of a cooperation agreement between the Penang Islamic Foundation (YIPP) and Idrissi International School. Also present were YIPP chief executive Dr Mohamad Sofee Razak and Idrissi founder Zaliza Alias.
Mohamad said the minimum age for Muslims to marry in Penang remained 16.
He said the state government would gather information and views from the relevant parties through the engagement sessions before considering its next course of action.

He was responding to reports that only Selangor and Kedah had amended their respective laws to raise the minimum marriage age for Muslims to 18, while other states were still subject to their own deliberations and legislative processes.

Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri was previously reported as saying that the government, through her ministry, would continue efforts to gradually standardise the minimum marriage age at 18 nationwide in close cooperation with state governments.
She said the effort would require engagement with state religious authorities, relevant agencies and stakeholders, as Islamic family law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments. — Bernama
cc1efc766ecf2d51: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 12 — The public is reminded to adhere to safety advice and take necessary precautions when dealing with floods, as well as to postpone all water-based recreational activities during the current North-east Monsoon (MTL) season.

Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Mohd Pisar Aziz said residents must immediately move to relief centres when instructed by the authorities or if rising floodwaters threaten their homes.
He cautioned the public against wading through flooded areas, whether on foot or by vehicle, as the depth of the water and strength of the currents could sweep anyone away.
“Parents are also reminded to monitor their children’s movements and prohibit them from playing in floodwaters to avoid the risk of drowning or other dangers,” he told Bernama.

He said that to avoid the risk of electric shocks, residents should switch off the main power supply before leaving their homes, provided it was safe to do so, and avoid touching electrical appliances in wet areas.
He also called on the public to stay clear of any severed or fallen electrical cables and to immediately report the matter to the authorities or Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd.

Mohd Pisar also advised the public to postpone all water-based recreational activities, including bathing, swimming, picnicking and camping near rivers, rapids, waterfalls and irrigation canals throughout the Northeast Monsoon season.

He said this was crucial due to the unpredictable weather conditions and persistent heavy rain in upstream catchment areas, which could cause water levels to rise abruptly and trigger sudden water surges that could claim lives within seconds.
“Water surges can happen in the blink of an eye following heavy rain in catchment areas, and the public should not wait until the water flowt becomes strong before taking action,” he added.

Mohd Pisar also reminded the public to remain vigilant always and stay updated on weather forecasts, comply with instructions from the authorities and heed safety warning signs placed at popular recreational spots.

He urged the public to immediately contact the emergency hotline at 999 in the event of an emergency or upon noticing early signs of a water surge to enable rescue operations to be launched without delay.
The public is also reminded to raise fire safety awareness at home by instilling safety-conscious practices from an early age.

He advised parents to keep an eye on their children to prevent them from playing with electrical switches or appliances unsupervised, while ensuring their hands are always dry and to avoid overloading electrical sockets.
“If a fire breaks out or smoke is detected in a home, occupants should leave immediately through a safe exit in a calm manner and assist family members without re-entering the premises,” he added.
He reminded the public not to attempt to put out a fire if the situation posed a threat to their lives, but instead leave the task to the fire and rescue personnel.
He stressed that fire prevention was a collective responsibility shared by all levels of society, complementing the department’s role as the nation’s main rescue agency. — Bernama
a54844b15eae4af3: MELAKA: Setiausaha Agung Umno Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki mengangkat manifesto Barisan Nasional (BN) sebagai manifesto yang bersifat inklusif, dengan inisiatif yang merangkumi dan meliputi semua kaum dan kelompok.
Sempena PRN Melaka, BN minggu lalu melancarkan manifesto 'Membina Masa Depan Melaka, Memakmurkan Negara' yang dirangka bersama Perikatan Nasional, menggariskan enam teras dan 113 inisiatif.
Pengerusi BN Melaka, Ab Rauf Yusoh menyifatkan manifesto itu 'manifestasi kesepakatan' BN-PN demi kepentingan rakyat Melaka, lapor Umno Online.
"Sudah tentu bila dikatakan rakyat Melaka, ia meliputi semua orang Melayu, orang Cina, orang India, kaum minoriti India Muslim, Siam, Orang Asli dan sebagainya," kata Asyraf.
"Manifesto BN tidak pernah memfokuskan kepada satu-satu kaum sahaja," katanya ketika ditemui selepas program bersama pengundi di Peringgit.

Antara tawaran yang diketengahkan dalam manifesto BN-PN adalah bil air percuma bagi penggunaan di bawah 20 meter padu sebulan, pembinaan 25,000 rumah mampu milik dalam tempoh lima tahun serta penyediaan perkhidmatan ambulans percuma.
Mengulas kerjasama BN-PN, Asyraf berkata gerak kerja di Melaka lebih menyeluruh berbanding ketika PRN Negeri Sembilan.

Asyraf yakin persefahaman itu boleh diperkukuh bagi menghadapi PRU akan datang, termasuk di negeri-negeri yang kini ditadbir PN.
PRN Melaka pada 14 Nov ini menyaksikan 28 kerusi DUN dipertandingkan, dengan BN bertanding di 23 kerusi manakala PN di lima kerusi.
817c8a9a721504c5: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The admission of international students to higher education institutions (HEIs) in the country continues to be subject to a stringent screening process to ensure that only qualified candidates are accepted, thereby preventing them from becoming a burden to the nation.

Higher Education director-general Datuk Prof Dr Azlinda Azman said particular emphasis was placed on cumulative grade point average (CGPA) and English language proficiency as key eligibility requirements to safeguard the quality of the country’s higher education.

“We want to ensure that quality standards remain at the highest level and not admit students indiscriminately, only for them to eventually create problems or become a burden to the country,” she told Bernama after officiating the Education Summit Kuala Lumpur here today.

Commenting on language requirements, Azlinda said all foreign students, including postgraduate students, were required to undergo a one-semester Bahasa Melayu course upon enrolment at local universities, particularly public universities (UA).
She said the measure would enable them to communicate in the national language in their daily affairs while fostering an understanding of the cultural diversity of the local community.
“Interestingly, most of these international students achieve excellent results in the subject because Bahasa Melayu is actually easy to learn,” she said.

Meanwhile, she said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) and the NAMA Foundation were actively mobilising efforts to secure funding contributors to offer full and partial scholarship schemes for international students.

Azlinda said the funding initiative could help cover students’ living expenses while driving the target of attracting 500,000 international students by 2035 under the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint (RPTM) 2026-2035, compared with approximately 170,000 currently.

She said student placements were also aligned with universities’ areas of specialisation, such as marine science at Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) and artificial intelligence (AI) at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) and Asia Pacific University (APU).

Meanwhile, Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) Chief Executive Officer Novie Tajuddin said Malaysia had made history as the first country in the world to establish a 24-hour International Student Arrival Centre (ISAC) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to facilitate the entry of foreign students.

“This is a unique initiative that has never been implemented by any other country and serves as an added value in terms of hospitality, distinguishing Malaysia from other study destinations,” he said.
He said the facility, officially introduced early this year, operated on a three-shift basis with the support of four dedicated immigration lanes.

In addition, Novie said the focus on student welfare had enabled Malaysia to rise from outside the world’s top 20 to the group of 14 leading countries (“Big 14”), while also ranking among the world’s top three in terms of annual and five-year growth rates in international student enrolment.

In 2025, EMGS received more than 95,000 international student applications, an increase of approximately 17 per cent compared with 2024, bringing the number of foreign students in the country to more than 167,000 from over 180 countries.
At today’s conference, six universities signed memoranda of agreement (MoAs) with EMGS and the NAMA Foundation to support funding and welfare for foreign students. — Bernama
fd433fb3c89e1861: PETALING JAYA: An unidentified woman was found dead in a river near a shopping centre in Sungai Petani, Kedah, today.
Kuala Muda police chief Hanyan Ramlan said the woman, who was naked, was believed to have died within the last 48 hours, based on the state of decomposition.
He said police, who received a call from the public about the discovery at about 1.30pm, have classified the case as sudden death pending an autopsy tomorrow.
“We have been unable to identify the woman or establish her age or race, due to the condition of the body,” he was quoted as saying by Bernama.
Hanyan said Kuala Muda police were conducting further checks in the district and neighbouring areas for reports involving missing women with similar characteristics.
“We estimate that the victim was 30 years old or older, but this has yet to be confirmed,” he said.
Hanyan urged members of the public who have missing family members to go to the nearest police station to assist with the investigation.
79de99d063b1affb: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Indian youths in Malaysia are feeling increasingly marginalised, facing systemic discrimination in education, employment, and housing that leaves many feeling politically alienated, according to a new report by think tank Iman Research.

The report, titled Kami Orang Sini Juga — Indian Youth Report, launched today, highlights that this demographic is an “under-mobilised constituency” whose concerns have long been overlooked by policymakers and the political establishment.

Based on in-depth interviews with 111 Indian youths nationwide, the study paints a stark picture of the hurdles these young Malaysians face from an early age, ranging from racial hostility in schools to precariousness in the housing and labour markets.
Iman Research researcher Shaleen Surendra highlighted that the findings serve as a critical wake-up call for those in power to address the growing disillusionment within the community.

“Indian youths are an under-mobilised constituency whose concerns have been ignored for too long. Through in-depth interviews, they described the discrimination faced, experiences of precarity towards their belonging, and being politically sidelined,” Shaleen said while presenting the findings.

“The report unpacks the repercussions of leaving these issues unaddressed, namely political alienation and distrust, which will shape the next election and the political landscape of the country,” she added.
From school to workforce
The research details a cycle of systemic failure.
Many Indian youths reported experiencing verbal and, in rarer cases, physical abuse from peers and teachers as early as their schooling years.
While Tamil primary schools were noted to offer a “temporary safety” net, they do not resolve the institutional structures that alienate these students.
The struggle continues into adulthood.
The report identifies that the matriculation system disproportionately affects youths from low-socioeconomic backgrounds, hindering their access to further education.

In the job and rental markets, these youths face inconsistent standards that often lead to outright rejection, forcing many to rely on informal networks that may not always be available to those from lower-income brackets.
Political tokenism and gang recruitment
The report also touches on the political landscape, noting that Indian youth votes are currently “up for grabs.”
However, the study warns that these voters are becoming increasingly savvy to “tokenistic representation.”
Participants expressed deep frustration with agencies such as the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (Mitra), which they perceive as lacking impact and reach.

The researchers warned that this disappointment should not be mistaken for apathy; rather, it is a sign that youths are demanding leaders—regardless of ethnicity—who will champion their rights through concrete action.
The consequences of this systemic exclusion remain significant.

The study highlighted that, without proper support systems, at-risk youths, particularly young Indian boys, are increasingly vulnerable to gang recruitment, which offers them a “false sense of safety and belonging.”
A call for structural reform
To bridge the gap between Indian youths and the rest of society, the report calls for comprehensive policy changes, including:
Educational reform: Shifting the matriculation quota system to a needs-based model and implementing sensitivity training for educators.
Legal protections: Introducing anti-discrimination legislation to govern hiring processes and rental standards.
Political inclusion: Establishing town halls and youth councils to bring young people directly into policy discussions and budgeting processes.
Civic engagement: Increasing transparency in government funding and promoting civic education programmes to mobilise youths beyond traditional party networks.
1bc4406ceb8eb745: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — A majority of PBA Holdings Bhd’s shareholders have approved Penang Water Supply Corporation’s (PBAPP) proposal to purchase a minimum of 300 million litres per day (MLD) of treated water from Perak starting in 2032.

PBA Holdings and PBAPP chairman Chow Kon Yeow said PBA has obtained the approval needed to fulfil a condition precedent in the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) between PBAPP and Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIP).

“At this general meeting, the board of directors’ proposal was approved by a majority vote, with 97.93 per cent voting in favour of PBAPP’s proposed purchase of treated water under the Penang-Perak Water Supply Scheme, as we have announced many times,” he said at a press conference after an extraordinary general meeting attended by shareholders today.
He said that after obtaining the approval, PBA will inform Bursa Malaysia and PAIP so that steps can be taken to commence the project.

“Under the agreement, we have a date for receiving the treated water — March 31, 2032. That is the date by which the project must be completed and treated water delivered to Penang, or to PBAPP, up to the Perak-Penang border and beyond that point, it is PBA’s responsibility to distribute the treated water we receive from Perak,” he said.
Chow, who is also Penang chief minister, said a group, representing minority shareholders, had submitted a letter in advance raising issues that was addressed during the meeting.
“Apart from the minority shareholder group, the other shareholders present did not raise any additional questions beyond those raised by the group,” he said.
As for the setting of water tariffs, Chow said this was already specified in the BWSA and that PAIP must fulfil one of the pre-conditions in obtaining approval from SPAN for the proposed tariff.

“That could also cause the project to fail. If Perak does not obtain SPAN’s approval for the proposed tariff, and for the capacity charge and other charges to be collected through the water tariff, the agreement will not proceed,” he said.
He said Perak has until 2035 to obtain SPAN’s approval for the tariff.

”If they cannot do so, we can say that we are walking away because SPAN has not approved it. They would then have to go back to SPAN and propose a new tariff until SPAN accepts the proposal,” he said.
He said this is a condition precedent of the agreement that Perak has to fulfil before the project can proceed.

861e01e051d3cad7: FRANKFURT, Nov 12 — German engineering giant Siemens posted record annual profit on Thursday and said it saw growth ahead as the artificial intelligence boom sweeps up European companies in its supply chain.

US tech giants such as Microsoft and Meta have together invested hundreds of billions of dollars in AI data centres, boosting the fortunes of companies like Siemens that make much of the electrical and cooling equipment needed to operate the sites.

Swiss competitor ABB in October posted order growth of 40 per cent for the three months to end-September, while France’s Schneider Electric in the same month said sales growth over the period had beaten expectations.

Reporting results for its fiscal year to end-September, Siemens said its core industrial profit, which strips out some effects such as last year’s sale of motor-maker Innomotics, rose 13 per cent to €13.3 billion (RM60.1 billion), or US$14.7 billion for the year.

Siemens said it expected further growth in the current business year, guiding for sales growth of between nine and 11 per cent across the company as well as broadly stable or higher profit margins at its two biggest divisions.

In the longer term, Siemens said it was now targeting sales growth of between seven and 11 per cent a year, up from six to nine, as well as annual earnings per share growth of at least 10 per cent, up from single-digit growth.
“Fiscal 2026 was an outstanding year for Siemens,” CEO Roland Busch said in a statement.
“We are providing an ambitious outlook for fiscal 2027 and are raising our group-level mid-term targets.”

For the fourth quarter, orders – an indicator of future sales – at Siemens’ smart infrastructure business rose 40 per cent to €8.67 billion (RM39.2 billion), helped by “numerous larger contract wins from data centre customers”, Siemens said.
Orders at Siemens’ digital industries division, which makes software for engineering and automation, rose 16 per cent over the same period to €6.41 billion (RM29 billion).
Under Busch, Siemens has pivoted towards higher-margin software products in recent years as part of its “Industrial AI” strategy. — AFP
6e968123ccf9bff9: PETALING JAYA: Misil dari Turki menjadi pilihan bagi menggantikan peluru berpandu antikapal (NSM) Norway untuk melengkapi sistem pertahanan kapal misi pesisir (LMS), kata Menteri Pertahanan Khaled Nordin.

65481771f9688521: TAIPEI, Nov 12 — A union representing workers at a Micron Technology plant in Taiwan said Thursday it will pull out of further talks with the US chip giant after “our defeat” in trying to secure a new profit-sharing deal.
Surging global demand for chips used in AI data centres has sent revenues soaring for firms like Micron, and as their earnings skyrocket, workers are calling for a bigger cut of profits.
Micron, which makes around 50-60 per cent of its memory chips in Taiwan, has been locked in weeks of talks over remuneration with a union representing hundreds of workers at its Taoyuan plant.
More than 2,000 employees had threatened to strike as they pushed for a bigger share of the company’s earnings.
In the end, only a handful of employees stopped working for one day.

“We formally acknowledge that our campaign to secure a profit-sharing system has not been successful, and we must continue our efforts in the future,” the union representing the Taoyuan workers said in a statement, acknowledging “our defeat”.
The union said its members could go ahead and sign an agreement with the company, adding that it will “no longer participate” in negotiations scheduled for November 17.

At Micron’s larger plant in Taichung, the union representing thousands of workers there signed an agreement with the company last month after they “reached consensus on a number of matters”, a joint statement said at the time.

5593d2aaccddb93f: LONDON, Nov 12 — Britain’s economy expanded in line with expectations in the third quarter, official data showed Thursday, as spending on the AI boom helped offset the fallout from the US-Iran war.

ff47cee33ad05fda: TAIPEI, Nov 12 — Taiwanese tech giant Foxconn on Thursday reported a record net profit for the third quarter, as the global buildout of data centres fuels demand for the AI servers needed to operate them.
The world’s largest electronics contract manufacturer has gone beyond making low-margin iPhones to producing AI servers for US tech titan Nvidia, as well as electric vehicles and robots.
Its shares and those of other tech firms plunged last week after the Democrats’ sweep of Congress in the US midterms would allow them to ramp up AI regulation and slow the data centre expansion.

Foxconn partner Nvidia has also weighed on sentiment, with US media reporting the company’s board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after revelations of his extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.
Foxconn said net profit for July-September hit NT$77.5 billion (RM9.8 billion), or US$2.4 billion (RM9.8 billion), up 34 per cent on-year.
The result beat estimates of NT$70.3 billion (RM8.9 billion) in a Bloomberg survey of analysts.
Revenue for the three months was up 39 per cent at NT$7.7 trillion (RM970 billion).
Chief Financial Officer David Huang said Foxconn’s “third-quarter revenue, operating income, net income, and earnings per share all reached record quarterly highs”.
“AI servers have become Foxconn’s most important growth driver,” Chairman Young Liu told a briefing.
Looking ahead, he said “we remain very confident in next year’s operations and believe growth will continue”.
But he warned of stubborn bottlenecks in the AI and consumer electronics supply chains, with overall demand “still expected to outpace supply heading into next year”.
That will mean “tight supply-demand conditions may persist for some time”, he said.
Foxconn has a longstanding partnership with Nvidia.
In one of their collaborations, the companies are working to build an “AI factory supercomputer” in Taiwan.
Governments and tech giants have been pouring huge sums into building data centres that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots, image generators and agents that can execute tasks.
The buildout has turbocharged business for Foxconn – which makes the servers used in the centres – but any slowdown could potentially hurt the company’s bottom line.
Data centres require large amounts of electricity, placing increased pressure on grids often still reliant on fossil fuels.
In many cases, they also ramp up strain on water resources used to cool computing equipment.
A backlash is growing worldwide against their environmental impacts, and there are also concerns over noise, pollution, their appearance and how many jobs the facilities actually create. — AFP

b5a7a069ea875674: There is a long list of people who have been, or still are, under detention in their own homes around the world.
Many are former heads of state or government. Apart from Najib Razak, we can count Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi and former French president Nicolas Sarkozy among them.
Like Najib, Sarkozy was convicted of a criminal offence. On the other hand, Suu Kyi is being detained for her opposition to the military dictatorship that continues to hold sway in Myanmar.
Another politician who also lived at home but as a prisoner was ex-Argentine president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner.
Unlike Malaysia, both Argentina and France already had provisions in their legal systems for home detention when their respective leaders — in this instance de Kirchner and Sarkozy — were sentenced.

In Argentina, the provision for house arrest goes back a long way — all the way back to 1886 when its first National Criminal Code was put in place. There have been several updates — in 1921, 1996 and subsequently in 2008.
According to Argentina.gob.ar, the official portal of the Argentine State, several conditions must be met before a prisoner qualifies for home detention.
He or she must be suffering from a terminal illness, or a malady that “cannot be adequately treated in prison” but does not require hospitalisation.
A person with a disability, making him vulnerable to inhumane or degrading treatment in a prison environment or any person aged over 70 also qualifies. So do pregnant women and caregiving mothers.
At age 72, de Kirchner qualifies on age alone.
In France, house arrest is provided for under Article 142-5 of the French Code of Criminal Procedure.

It states that a person convicted of a criminal offence and sentenced to a year or less in jail can be confined to his home under strict conditions. The prisoner must also show that he does not pose a flight risk.
Sarkozy was sentenced to three years but qualified anyway because two of those three years were suspended.
As far as we know, Najib is neither ill nor pregnant. He does not have any young child to watch over either.
At age 76, former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Isa Samad is still serving out his six-year prison sentence for corruption. Najib is three years younger than him.
Even if we pick a leaf or two from the Argentine and French playbooks on home detention, Najib does not qualify on any front.

In September, Najib was granted a conditional pardon by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong under which he could serve out the remainder of his six-year sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.
The condition was that he paid the RM50 million fine. Umno managed to raise the sum and the fine was paid on Nov 6.
Najib is already home to continue serving his sentence, but it is not too late to start thinking about putting in place provisions for house arrest.
Chances are there will be more to come.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
4731a07ed3bf1bfc: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where all the victims are self-owned. This week, we welcome you to a London hotel where you could check out its admin credentials for a booking website just by walking past the front desk.

Our story comes courtesy of Neycho Tepavicharov, co-founder of Flashcloud, a Delaware-based web hosting company. He was staying at a hotel in London when he noticed a shocking breach of basic security protocols by management, who were a little too hospitable with their credentials.

As he was passing through the lobby, Tepavicharov noticed that the door behind the front desk was open and, inside that back room, there was a whiteboard. On the whiteboard, written in plain English, were the hotel’s Booking.com administrative username and password.

Anyone near the desk could clearly see the login information, and if they didn’t have time to write it down, they could have snapped a picture for later use. As Tepavicharov explains, there’s plenty of mischief you could perform with these credentials.

“With that login, someone could change or cancel reservations, see guests’ names and contact details, or message guests pretending to be the hotel,” he said. “Fake 'please confirm your payment' messages sent from compromised hotel accounts are a well-known scam.”

An attacker could potentially exploit that access to disrupt hotel operations or target guests with convincing scams. Whether the exposed credentials alone would have been enough to access the account would depend on its security settings.
Tepavicharov decided to play the role of good samaritan and warn the hotel’s manager that the business was endangering itself by showing everyone its password.

“I asked to speak with the manager and showed him what I’d seen. He was mortified and very grateful,” Tepavicharov said. “Nobody on staff had thought of it as a risk. It was just the easiest way for the whole team to share one login.”
After Tepavicharov talked to the manager, not only did the hotel change its ways, but it also moved its website to his hosting service, Flashcloud.
Tepavicharov notes that there are plenty of takeaways from this incident. Most important: give each user dedicated credentials with their own separate login, and use multi-factor authentication.

“The lesson is an old one, but it keeps happening,” he said. “Shared logins end up written somewhere convenient. Give each staff member their own login, turn on two-factor authentication, and keep passwords in a password manager, not on the wall.” ®
05a995930b01ced5: HONG KONG, Nov 12 — Asian stocks fell Thursday as investors kept a nervous eye on Nvidia whose influential boss Jensen Huang faces a probe into an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.

Companies linked to the artificial intelligence sector have enjoyed a healthy bounce in recent days after last week’s selloff sparked by regulatory concerns following the Democratic sweep of Congress.

The upcoming IPO of Anthropic and positive earnings from the likes of ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and data centre operator CoreWeave – which soothed worries about its financial health – have reinforced optimism.
Chipmakers SK hynix, Samsung, Kioxia and TSMC have led the surge in Asia, even amid rising expectations for a series of US interest rate hikes.
All three main indexes on Wall Street ended on another strong note Wednesday.
But Asia’s run-up came to an end despite a healthy start to the day.
Tokyo, Seoul, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Sydney, Singapore, Mumbai, Bangkok and Manila all dropped, though there were gains in Jakarta and Wellington.

Traders’ nerves are being tested by the crisis at Nvidia, with co-founder and CEO Huang facing the boot after he admitted a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo in spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with the company’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.
The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter.

Huang has built Nvidia to be one of the world’s biggest and most important companies, designing advanced chips crucial to the AI buildout that has helped drive stock markets to record highs and boosted economies around the world.
Succession concerns
“Nvidia has spent years convincing investors that it is one of the most important companies in the AI revolution,” wrote Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets.
“Now, the biggest question surrounding the company is not about its chips, competitors or earnings.
“It is about its founder.”
She said Huang was key to the firm’s future, including dealings with governments.
“Nvidia’s technological advantage would not disappear with his departure,” she added.
“Its CUDA software ecosystem, product capabilities and customer relationships remain formidable strengths.
“But an abrupt exit without a credible succession plan could force investors to reassess how much of Nvidia’s future depends on Huang personally.”
Nvidia’s shares slid more than eight per cent in after-hours US trade, and are down around 20 per cent since news of the affair broke at the end of last month.
Oil prices inched down as investors kept tabs on the Middle East crisis, with hopes still high that the US and Iran can reach a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
On currency markets the rupiah hit a record low against the dollar as traders rushed into the US unit on expectations the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates into the new year.
Asia’s worst-performing currency this year weakened to as much as 18,253 to the greenback in afternoon trade, spurring the Indonesian central bank to intervene to provide support.

The drop came just before the country’s vice president resigned in the midst of a scandal over his high school diploma, adding to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires.

01f80b60358b266d: LOS ANGELES, Nov 12 — For nearly two decades, Kimberly Powell has been the person Nvidia sends out to explain what its chips can do for medicine.
This week, she became a name nobody at the company wanted to see in the headlines.

Powell, 48, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, was named by the New York Times (NYT) yesterday as the senior executive with whom chief executive Jensen Huang allegedly had an extramarital relationship, a claim neither has confirmed.
The NYT, citing five people who worked at the company, said Powell reported to Huang.
Her sudden prominence is the latest twist in a scandal that has engulfed one of the world’s most valuable technology companies in less than a week.
An engineer first
Powell’s route to Silicon Valley’s inner circle began with circuit boards, not boardrooms.
While studying electrical engineering at Northeastern University, she took an internship at a medical imaging company, an early brush with the field she would later help Nvidia enter.
She worked as a hardware engineer at Dome Imaging Systems and as a product manager for diagnostic display systems at Planar Systems before moving to Nvidia.
She joined in 2008 with a narrow brief: to make Nvidia’s graphics processors the accelerator of choice for medical imaging equipment.
From there she took on the company’s higher education and research business, its AI Labs and Inception, its programme for AI start-ups.
Her LinkedIn profile shows a promotion to senior director of AI business development in 2016.
CNBC has reported that she has led the healthcare group since 2017.
Under her watch, the business grew to include platforms such as BioNeMo for AI-driven biology and drug discovery.
“AI is the biggest technological breakthrough of our lifetime,” she has said.
She has also carried that message abroad, headlining a fireside chat in Singapore in 2019 and, according to Taiwan’s Liberty Times, leading an Nvidia team to medical centres in Taiwan in 2024.
How the spotlight arrived
The attention came in two stages, a few days apart.

Last Sunday, Huang admitted in a note to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, and Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation into reports that he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
The relationship he admitted to was widely reported to be with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and a former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security, an allegation Beijing has rejected.
Then came yesterday’s report.
The NYT said Powell is among the roughly 60 executives who report directly to Huang, and that both are married to other people.

The NYT also said Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel in San Jose during Nvidia’s annual developer GPU Technology Conference in San Jose, California, in March, but added that it had not seen any footage.
Huang and Nvidia have declined to comment, and Powell did not respond to NYT.
Nvidia shares fell 8.3 per cent in after-hours trading that evening and continues to slide a day later.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to meet to decide Huang’s future in the company he co-founded.
Why it matters
Nvidia sits at the centre of the global race in artificial intelligence, and its chips are a pressure point in US-China technology rivalry.
Huang has no publicly known succession plan.
The company is due to report third-quarter results in five days, on November 17.
For the board, a relationship between the CEO and a direct report, if the allegations are borne out, raises questions of governance and workplace conduct that go beyond their private lives.
Powell’s husband
The Daily Beast reported that Powell is married to Graham Gerade, 54, who is listed as a co-inventor of a medical imaging viewer application on a US patent.
Gerade is not accused of any wrongdoing.
For Powell, the episode puts a career built on two decades of engineering and healthcare work in front of a global audience, and for now it rests on a single newspaper report.
Malay Mail has not independently verified the allegations.
927895df727f2703: GENEVA: The US head of the UN telecommunications agency resoundingly won a second four-year mandate on Thursday, obtaining a key objective for the Trump administration which is trying to counter China within the global body.

Doreen Bogdan-Martin, who ran unopposed, won the election for secretary-general of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) - the UN body that sets standards for new technologies - with 164 votes out of 173 votes.

"Together, we can make sure the digital future leaves no one behind," she said at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, Qatar, referring to her objective of connecting the 2 billion people around the world who remain offline.

0cf2cdf6ee81ef32: Keeping sensitive data within national borders might satisfy a residency requirement. But does it mean your organization is genuinely in control?
Not necessarily. Data could be stored locally while remaining subject to another jurisdiction's laws, dependent on overseas service providers or exposed to disruption beyond your control.

For enterprise IT teams, that distinction is becoming harder to ignore. Geopolitical tensions, evolving regulations and the growing use of AI are forcing organizations to reconsider what data sovereignty means in practice. Yet translating those concerns into a workable strategy is another matter.
And simply throwing more money at the problem won't necessarily solve it.

In The Register's on-demand webinar, Data Sovereignty By Design, moderator Tim Phillips speaks with Patrick Smith, Field CTO for EMEA at Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, about moving beyond compliance checklists and taking a more strategic approach to data control.

Drawing on findings from Everpure's research, Smith explores a curious disconnect: organizations are increasing their investment in sovereignty initiatives, yet many still lack a coordinated strategy. Some of the risks attracting the most attention aren't necessarily those receiving the greatest investment.

The discussion examines why sovereignty shouldn't be treated as an IT-only responsibility. Decisions about which data needs protection, which services must remain operational and what level of risk is acceptable require input from business leaders, security, procurement and legal teams.

There's also the question of priorities. Not every workload needs the same sovereign controls, and attempting to protect everything equally can make an already complicated challenge considerably harder.

Smith explains the concept of the "minimum viable company," identifying the critical services, applications and data an organization needs to keep operating through disruption. He also considers why visibility into data access, supplier dependencies and potential exit strategies should influence technology decisions from the outset.
For IT leaders trying to turn sovereignty from an abstract boardroom concern into something actionable, the conversation offers useful questions to take back to their organizations.
Because knowing where your data sits is one thing. Knowing whether you can maintain control when circumstances change is quite another.

17def1a151ab70e7: Every so often a flaw comes along that shows how fast the ground can shift under IT and security teams. PHP2Shell, a pair of critical flaws in PHP, was one of them. Details leaked before the planned disclosure, frontier AI helped researchers find the flaws, and PHP shipped fixes the next day. For many teams, though, the patch was the easy part. So what does it take to respond at that speed, and where should teams begin?
What does governed autonomous IT look like in practice?

Picture a loop. Software finds where a risk lives and ranks what matters most. It proposes a fix, then, inside limits people define, carries it out and checks that it worked. Routine, low-risk actions can run on their own. Higher-impact ones wait for a person to approve. A few are never handed over at all. Each step leaves a record that someone can review and reverse.
What challenges do IT and security teams face today?

Three problems keep coming up. The first is visibility. PHP2Shell reportedly sat undetected for more than a decade. For these two flaws, the fix was a version upgrade. The hard part was finding every copy of PHP, including copies bundled inside other software or extracted by hand onto Windows machines that never registered as installed applications. Then teams had to work out which copies the internet could reach and check for signs of earlier attack. An inventory built from a periodic snapshot can't answer those questions on the day they matter.

The second is tool-hopping. Answering "where does this run, and can the internet reach it?" often means pivoting across an asset inventory, a vulnerability scanner and an external attack surface tool, each with its own view. Every hop adds delay. Every console is another chance to disagree with the last.

The third is pace. Several security firms reported exploitation attempts before PHP released its fixes, and Cloudflare reported early attacks hours ahead of the patch. Frontier AI models helped find PHP2Shell, and in April Anthropic said its Claude Mythos Preview model had found thousands of previously unknown flaws across every major operating system and browser. With models like these in the picture, the old rhythm of disclose, patch and verify assumes a gap that keeps shrinking.
Put an AI agent on top of stale, fragmented data and these problems don't go away. They scale.
Why does real-time endpoint data make autonomy trustworthy?
Endpoints are where work happens and where many attacks end up, so they are the ground truth for any decision about the estate. Four qualities make that data a sound foundation for autonomous action:
Accuracy: Live data from the endpoints themselves, not a snapshot that was true last week.
Speed: A short path from question to action, with no hopping between tools to reconcile answers.
Control: Approvals and an audit trail, plus the ability to roll back, so any automated action can be reviewed and reversed.
Shared truth: IT operations, security and the system of record working from one view, rather than arguing over whose data is right.
Matt Psencik, a threat research engineer at Tanium, put the visibility problem bluntly when PHP2Shell broke: "The installations that worry me most are the ones a security team doesn't know it owns."
How does AI fit in?

AI sits on both sides of this. It helped researchers find the PHP2Shell flaws, and attackers can use it to build exploits too. For defenders, AI works best as the operator and the interface: it takes a plain-language question, works out what to ask of the data, and proposes or carries out the next step. But it is only as good as the data it is grounded in. A fluent answer built on outdated information is still wrong, just more confidently so. Keeping people in the loop where stakes are high is what makes automation safe to expand.
What are the practical first steps?
Teams don't need to hand over the keys all at once. Start here:

Find every copy: Don't stop at the installed-applications list. PHP2Shell showed that software bundled inside other products can slip past it. Compare your CMDB against what is really on your network and record exact versions.

Draw the lines: Rank systems by what the internet can reach, then decide which response actions run automatically, which need approval and which are never delegated. Write it down before an agent needs it.
Pilot one low-risk workflow: Pick something contained, build approval into it, and read the audit trail before widening the scope.

Teams can also shorten the pilot with a partner. World Wide Technology (WWT), a Tanium partner, works with many large organizations on technology rollouts and hosts a Tanium lab in its Advanced Technology Center, where customers can test an approach hands-on before moving it into production.

That second problem, the hopping, is the one Tanium Atlas was built to close. Instead of moving between consoles, an operator asks a plain-language question, gets an answer from live endpoint data, and acts on it inside limits the team sets, with every action recorded. 4dcaee04b6caac45: The school gardens are helping alleviate food insecurity while providing learning opportunities and empowering community members
Originally published on Global Voices
Students of Blessed Bilingual Education Centre preparing the farm. Photo by Support Humanity Cameroon. Used with permission.

Students of Blessed Bilingual Education Centre in Ebang, Cameroon’s Centre Region, have recorded their first harvest of the 2026–2027 school year. Through the Climate Change and Innovation Club, an initiative introduced in 2024 by Support Humanity Cameroon (SUHUCAM) to connect environmental education with practical action, students planted huckleberry in their school garden at the start of the academic year in September. Like them, pupils in Cameroon’s North West Region are managing school gardens and growing food using regenerative practices such as minimal tillage, composting, organic manure and fruit-tree grafting.

Cameroon continues to face a decade-long humanitarian crisis, contributing to food insecurity in the Anglophone regions and Far North, while displacing thousands of families. Earlier this year, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies reported worsening hunger among nearly 6,000 Cameroonian households following an assessment. More than 3.3 million people were struggling to find enough food, while about 64 percent of households experienced severe food insecurity.

Children are among those affected. Nationwide, 29 percent of children under five experience chronic malnutrition. Beyond its nutritional consequences, food insecurity can also affect children’s ability to learn and participate in school activities.

According to the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), hunger can impair concentration and memory and affect classroom attendance. In February 2026, the organisation reported that only 2.8 percent of primary school pupils in Cameroon received a free hot meal at school, highlighting the limited reach of school lunch programmes.
Conflict, climate-related disasters, agricultural losses and rising staple food prices are among the main drivers of this crisis.
School gardens in action
To combat persistent food insecurity, educators and nonprofit organisations are partnering to teach children how to grow their own food.

In Bamenda, North West region of Cameroon, the Youth Association for Climate Action (YACA) runs the ADAPT Programme, which engages 70 pupils from two nursery and primary schools. Created after a survey revealed that few schools had gardens or provided environmental education, the ADAPT Club has established gardens with five sections: nurseries, vegetables, fruit trees, composting and tubers.

Muluh Kelly Vughose, Programme coordinator for ADAPT, says pupils are involved in more than just planting. “Our volunteers, together with the teachers and pupils, designed each garden. Children are also involved in learning basic agricultural skills like plantain propagation and grafting of fruit trees.” The club holds two sessions each week, lasting about two hours.

In the same region, in Nkambe and neighbouring villages, pupils from six primary and two secondary schools are learning agricultural skills through the Smart School Gardens Project, launched by Youth Development Organisation – Yodo Cameroon. Schools have received wheelbarrows, watering cans and compost manure to support the project.

“During the two years of implementation, I have watched these pupils and students care for plants from seed germination until harvest,” says Ekoaba Cevie, Yodo Cameroon’s Programme Coordinator. The gardens produce cabbage, huckleberry, carrots and Irish potatoes.

Meanwhile, SUHUCAM’s regenerative school garden programme in the Centre region combines fruit trees, including guava, soursop, orange and papaya, with plantains and produce such as huckleberry, cabbage and waterleaf. Through these activities, pupils are learning techniques such as composting, plant propagation and grafting.

Children are embracing the school gardens with enthusiasm, discovering the importance of food production and sustainability through practical experience. Queeninver Ngwangung, SUHUCAM’s Youth and Advocacy Lead, explains:

“Rather than simply teaching students about sustainable agriculture, food security or climate action, we give them opportunities to practice these concepts,” she said. “Through growing food, managing organic waste and caring for their gardens, we have observed that students have learnt that environmental solutions can begin with everyday actions within their own schools.”

For Amang Mael, a Form Three student, seeing vegetables grow on an abandoned plot behind his school has been particularly exciting. “Since we planted the vegetables, I have been so eager to harvest. We add organic manure to all our crops so they can be healthy.”

Another student, Kouba Princesse, believes the garden can contribute to the fight against hunger. “Now that I know how to grow my own vegetables, I will not have to depend on buying from the market all the time,” she says. Some kids have taken the practice home, where they maintain small gardens and use plastic bottles for drip irrigation during the dry season. Other students also say the experience has sparked an interest in pursuing careers in agriculture.
Supporting community nutrition

In 2025, the ADAPT Club produced approximately 45 kilogrammes of dry compost from biodegradable waste. At the end of each planting cycle, YACA organises a Mini School Garden Market Day, where parents and community members can buy the harvest. “Income gained is reinvested in the next planting cycle,” says Muluh Kelly.

At SUHUCAM, the harvests serve nutritional and educational purposes. Students eat fruits from the gardens, while vegetables are sold to purchase seeds and fund their continued management. Some students take extra produce home to establish household gardens.
After two years with two regenerative school garden cycles, SUHUCAM’s Climate Change and Innovation Club has benefitted thousands of households and planted over 400 trees.

In Nkambe, pupils involved in Yodo Cameroon’s project also sell their harvests to community members at affordable prices. The proceeds have helped schools purchase basic educational materials, including chalk and exercise books. Ekoaba Cevie, Yodo Cameroon’s project manager says:

The gardens have become practical outdoor classrooms. Not only are the children learning new agricultural skills, but they are also gaining an appreciation for nature, responsible environmental practices and sustainable resource management.

The nutritional potential of school-based production is also evident in other initiatives. In 2025, an integrated school production programme supported by FAO in Cameroon’s East and South regions established 18 school gardens. The programme produced 236,859 kilogrammes of vegetables, alongside eggs and fish, helping provide weekly healthy meals to 10,833 students. Children, teachers and community members also received training in sustainable agriculture, hygiene and nutrition.

Nkimih Clinton, a researcher at the Institute of Agricultural Research for Development (IRAD), says regenerative practices, such as those deployed in the community gardens, can improve soil health and support sustainable agriculture. Composting, mulching, crop rotation and organic manure, he explains, “can contribute to maintaining the health of pieces of land” for crop production. However, he cautions against expecting small-scale school gardens to eliminate hunger entirely.

Although they may not provide all the food pupils need, they can improve dietary quality by supplying vegetables, legumes and fruits rich in essential vitamins and minerals. “School gardens can be used as a source of production of micro-nutrients to complement basic staples (cassava, maize, rice) provided by parents,” Clinton says.
Challenges to overcome

Despite their benefits, maintaining school gardens remains difficult. Programme coordinators say unpredictable rainfall makes it harder to plan planting activities and sustain crop production. Changing weather conditions can also contribute to pest outbreaks and seed shortages.

Maintaining the gardens during school holidays is another challenge, as pupils are less available to care for the crops. These difficulties can interrupt children’s opportunities to follow the entire production cycle, from planting to harvesting. Expanding the initiatives will therefore require coordinated support from government officials, agricultural research institutions and development partners.
Schools need funding, reliable water supply, farming tools, quality seeds and technical assistance to maintain productive gardens throughout the year.
Government and policy support

Cameroon has previously taken steps to promote environmental education in schools. In 2018, the Ministry of Secondary Education and the Israeli Ambassador to Cameroon launched a Green School campaign that planted 300 trees in 30 schools.

In May 2023, the country launched the second phase of the Classes Vertes project, a three-year initiative developed by FAO in partnership with the Special Council Support Fund for Mutual Assistance (FEICOM) and several government ministries. Targeting 80 schools across the Far North, North, Adamawa, East and South regions, the programme sought to promote vegetable production, fish farming and poultry farming to improve children’s access to nutritious food. It also included tree planting and initiatives to build school canteens, water, sanitation, and hygiene facilities, with an allocated budget of approximately FCFA 722 million (USD 1.2 million).

The government’s commitment to improving children’s access to nutritious food is also reflected in its National School Feeding Strategy for 2025–2030, which aims to expand school meals and strengthen links between schools and local food producers.

Officials hope the program will reach one million learners by 2030. In July 2026, the government, through the Ministry of Basic Education, signed a EUR 3.6 million (USD 4 million) agreement with the World Food Programme (WFP) to expand home-grown school feeding in the Adamawa, East and Far North regions. The 2026–2029 programme is expected to provide nutritious meals to nearly 11,000 children in ten public primary schools while creating market opportunities for 600 smallholder farmers.

Meanwhile, experts believe school gardens can be replicated across Cameroon but stress that their implementation must reflect the country’s different agro-ecological zones. Rather than adopting a uniform approach, schools need solutions suited to their agro-ecological zones.

While school gardens may not independently resolve Cameroon’s food insecurity challenges, they offer opportunities to strengthen children’s nutritional knowledge, promote sustainable agriculture and encourage household food production. Their long-term impact, however, will depend on sustained investment, technical support and policies that enable more schools to establish and maintain these initiatives.
Written by Sandra Tuombouh

610b74066fe65872: LOS ANGELES, Nov 12 — Chip giant Nvidia’s board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to US media.

The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered with reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data centre executive who has been accused by US intelligence of working for China’s Ministry of State Security.

With Huang unexpectedly on the back foot, and no known plan of succession at Nvidia, the field is wide open for a variety of replacements to lead one of the key AI players should the board decide to oust Huang.
Here are some of the names being suggested most frequently as Huang’s potential successor.
Internal hire
With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports.
Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth.
Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data centre clients.
He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand.
Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick.
A family affair
Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession.
His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts.
As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH.
Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor.
He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division.

Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection — not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD.
Tech CEO swap
Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang.
Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press.

Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped. — AFP
